With those arrows, he caused their heads to fly. When they fell dead thus, the rest of them ran helter-skelter. Chasing the enemies away like a lion chases stray deer, Bhima faced the grandson of Hridika (Krutavarma).

units.sanskrit:
विजित्य हार्दिक्यमथाशु भीमो विद्रावयामास वरूथिनीं ताम्।
सम्प्रेषयन् सर्वनराश्‍वकुञ्जरान् यमाय यातो हरिपार्थपार्श्‍वम् ॥ २६/१३७॥
दृष्ट्वैव कृष्णविजयौ परमप्रहृष्टस्ताभ्यां निरीक्षित उत प्रतिभाषितश्‍च।
सञ्ज्ञां नृपस्य स ददावपि सिंहनादात् श्रुत्वा परां मुदमवाप स चाग्र्यबुद्धिः ॥ २६/१३८॥
भीमस्य नानदत एव महास्वनेन विण्मूत्रशोणितमथो मृतिमापुरेके।

भीतेषु सर्वनृपतिष्वमुमाप तूर्णं कर्णो विकर्णमुखरा अपि धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥ २६/१३९॥
हत्वा विकर्णमुत तत्र च चित्रसेनं सञ्चूर्णितं प्रविदधे रथमर्कसूनोः।
घोरैः शरैः पुनरपि स्म समर्द्यमानः कर्णोऽपयानमकरोद् द्रुतमेव भीमात् ॥ २६/१४०॥
आश्‍वास्य चैव सुचिरं पुनरेव भीमं युद्धाय याति धृतराष्ट्रसुतैस्तथाऽन्यैः।
तांश्‍चैव तत्र विनिहत्य तथैव कर्णो व्यश्‍वायुधः कृत उतापययौ क्षणेन ॥ २६/१४१॥
विकर्णचित्रसेनाद्या एवं वीरतमाः सुताः।
कर्णस्य पश्यतो भीमबाणकृत्तशिरोधराः ॥ २६/१४२॥
निपेतुर्धृतराष्ट्रस्य रथेभ्यः पृथिवीतले।
त्रयोविंशतिरेवात्र कर्णसाहाय्यकारिणः ॥ २६/१४३॥
एकविंशतिवारं च व्यश्‍वसूतरथध्वजः।
गाढमभ्यर्द्दितस्तीक्ष्णैः शरैर्भीमेन संयुगे ॥ २६/१४४॥
units.english:
When he obstructed by using arrows, Bhima quickly rendered him chariot-less and killed his horses and charioteer. Having been hurt very badly by Vrikodara, Krutavarma gave up battle and immediately left.

As soon as he won against Krutavarma, Bhima started scattering the enemies. Killing all foot- soldiers, horses and elephants, he got close to Sri Krishna and Arjuna. Bhima became very pleased seeing Sri Krishna and Vijaya. They too saw him and engaged in conversation. Through a ferocious roar, Bhima indicated to Dharmaraja (about Arjuna’s safety). Hearing that, Dharmaraja, possessing excellent intellect, rejoiced greatly.

When Bhima gave that leonine roar, the loud sound caused many Kaurava soldiers to urinate and excrete (out of fear). Others vomited blood and many died too. When all the Kings became scared then, Karna rushed towards Bhima. Vikarna and the other Kauravas too came there.

In that battle, Bhima killed Vikarna and Chitrasena. Later, he smashed the chariot of the son of Surya (Karna). When Bhima started hitting him repeatedly with fiery arrows, Karna immediately ran away far from there.

After recovering for a long time, Karna proceeded again against Bhima along with many Kauravas. Bhima killed all those Kauravas and destroyed Karna’s horses. He broke Karna’s weapons. Karna, once again, ran away from there quickly.

Even as Karna kept watching, twenty three brave sons of Dhritharashtra, including Vikarna and Chitrasena, fell down from their chariots, their heads being cut off by Bhima’s arrows. All of them had come to help Karna.

In that battle, Karna lost his horses, charioteer, chariot and flags twenty one times, due to the fiery arrows of Bhima. He got hurt on his body too.

units.sanskrit:
प्राणसंशयमापन्नः सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः।
रणं त्यक्त्वा प्रदुद्राव रुदन् दुःखात् पुनःपुनः ॥ २६/१४५॥
द्वाविंशतिमयुद्धे तु रामदत्तं सुभास्वरम्।
अभेद्यं रथमारुह्य विजयं धनुरेव च ॥ २६/१४६॥
तद्दत्तमेव सङ्गृह्य तूणौ चाक्षयसायकौ।
आससाद रणे भीमं कर्णो वैकर्तनो वृषा ॥ २६/१४७॥
सुघोर आसीत् स तयोर्विमर्दो भीमस्य कर्णस्य च दीर्घकालम्।
आकाशमाच्छादयतोः शरौघैः परस्परं चैव सुरक्तनेत्रयोः ॥ २६/१४८॥
ततो भीमो महाबाहुः सहजाभ्यां च संयुतम्।
त्वां तु कुण्डलवर्मभ्यां शक्नुयां हन्तुमञ्जसा ॥ २६/१४९॥
इति ज्ञापयितुं तस्य कुण्डले कवचं तथा।
शरैरुत्कृत्य समरे पातयामास भूतले ॥ २६/१५०॥
एवं तान्यपकृष्याहं हन्यां त्वामिति वेदयन्।
पुनश्‍च बहुभिस्तीक्ष्णैः शरैरेनं समार्दयत् ॥ २६/१५१॥
ततस्तु भीमस्य बभूव बुद्धिरस्पर्धिनः सर्वजयो हि दत्तः।
अमुष्य रामेण नच स्पृधाऽयं कर्णो मया युद्ध्यति कृच्छ्रगो ह्ययम् ॥ २६/१५२॥
units.english:
Worrying about his life, Karna kept leaving the battlefield out of sorrow and crying repeatedly even as everyone was watching.

In the twenty second duel, Karna ascended an extremely radiant and impregnable chariot given by Sri Parashurama. He picked up a bow called Vijaya given also by him. Bringing along two quivers that would never run out of arrows, he faced Bhima with great anger.

An extremely terrifying battle took place between Bhima and Karna for a long time. Both of them fought each other with blood-red eyes, covering the sky with clusters of arrows.

“I am fully capable of killing you even if you had possessed the kavacha and kundala you were born with” – in order to convey such a message the mighty armed Bhimasena cut off Karna’s ear-rings and protective shield with his arrows and felled them on the ground in that battle.

Felling them thus and conveying the message “I can kill you” Bhima tormented Karna once again with great many sharp arrows.

Bhima then thought – “He has been granted a boon by Sri Parashurama that he shall win against everyone if he doesn’t battle with a sense of competition. Being in danger from me, he is not fighting with me in competition”.

units.sanskrit:
तथाऽपि मे भगवानत्यनुग्रहाज्जयं ददात्यात्मवचो विहाय।
मया तु मान्यं वचनं हरेः सदा तस्माद् दास्ये विवरं त्वद्य शत्रोः ॥ २६/१५३॥
एवं स्मृत्वा तेन रन्ध्रे प्रदत्ते कर्णोऽस्त्रवीर्येण धनुर्न्यकृन्तत्।
रश्मीन् हयानां च ततो रथं स तत्याज नैजं बलमेव वेदयन् ॥ २६/१५४॥
न मे रथाद्यैर्धनुषाऽपि कार्यमित्येव सञ्ज्ञापयितुं वृकोदरः।
खमुत्पपातोत्तमवीर्यतेजा रथं च कर्णस्य समास्थितः क्षणात् ॥ २६/१५५॥
भीतस्तु कर्णो रथकूबरे तदा व्यलीयताधः स वृकोदरो रथात्।
अवप्लुतो ज्ञापयितुं स्वशक्तिं निरायुधत्वेऽप्यरिनिग्रहादौ ॥ २६/१५६॥
नैच्छद् ग्रहीतुं विनिहन्तुमेव वा रथं धनुर्वाऽस्य रणेऽपहर्तुम्।
द्रोणस्य यद्वत् पूर्वमतीव शक्तोऽप्यमानयद् रामवचोऽस्य भक्त्या ॥ २६/१५७॥
सत्यां कर्तुं वासवेश्‍च प्रतिज्ञां सम्मानयन् वैष्णवत्वाच्च कर्णम्।
दातुं रन्ध्रं सूर्यजस्य प्रयातः शरक्षेपार्थं दूरमतिष्ठदत्र ॥ २६/१५८॥
ततः कर्णो दूरगतं वृकोदरं सम्मानयन्तं रामवाक्यं विजानन्।
शरैरविध्यत् स च तानवारयद् गजैर्मृतैस्तांश्‍च चकर्त कर्णः ॥ २६/१५९॥
व्यसून् गजान् प्रक्षिपन्तं समेत्य संस्पृश्य चापेन वचश्‍च दुष्टम्।
संश्रावयामास सुयोधनस्य प्रीत्यै प्रजानन्नपि तस्य वीर्यम् ॥ २६/१६०॥
units.english:
“Still, Bhagavan Parashurama, due to his extreme grace, is granting me victory without considering his own boon. However, I have to respect Sri Hari’s words at all times. Therefore let me provide space (an opportunity) for Karna now”.

Thinking thus, when Bhima allowed it, Karna cut Bhima’s bow with the prowess of astras he possessed. He cut off the ropes of the horses too. Later, in order to display his true strength, Bhima gave up his chariot and alighted.

In order to let everyone know that he needed neither the chariot nor the bow, that excellent warrior Vrikodara jumped into the sky and instantly landed on Karna’s chariot.

A frightened Karna hid below the pole of the chariot. Vrikodara then, having shown that he could control the enemy even when without a weapon, jumped out of the chariot.

Even though Bhima was fully capable of capturing Karna, or kill him, or take away his chariot or bow in battle, or to do to him what he did to Drona, he respected Sri Parashurama’s words out of devotion.

In order to make Arjuna’s vow come true, and because Karna was a Vaishnava, Bhima went a little away from there and stood, so he could release arrows at him.

Then, knowing that Bhimasena has stood there to respect the words of Sri Parashurama, Karna started hitting him with arrows. Bhima stopped his arrows using dead elephants. Karna started cutting off the dead corpses of the elephants.

Approaching Bhima who was throwing dead elephants, Karna pierced him with the edge of his bow. Even though he knew Bhima’s valour very well, he spoke dirty words in order to please Duryodhana.

units.sanskrit:
संश्रावयन्तं वचनानि रूक्षाण्यपाहनद् बाणवरैस्तदाऽर्जुनः।
स वर्महीनः पार्थबाणाभितप्तो व्यपागमद् भीम आपात्मयानम् ॥ २६/१६१॥
कर्णो भीमे वासवीं नैव शक्तिं विमोक्तुमैच्छन्नैव बीभत्सुतोऽन्यान्।
हन्यामिति प्राह यतः स कुन्त्यै यद्यप्यवध्यः स तयाऽपि भीमः ॥ २६/१६२॥
नारायणास्त्रं शिरसि प्रपातितं न यस्य लोमाप्यदहच्छिरस्थितम्।
किं तस्य शक्तिः प्रकरोति वासवी तथाऽन्यदप्यस्त्रशस्त्रं महच्च ॥ २६/१६३॥
भीमः कर्णरथं प्राप्तः शक्तिं नादातुमैच्छत।
अभिप्रायं केशवस्य जानन् हैडिम्बमृत्यवे ॥ २६/१६४॥
ततः कर्णोऽन्यमास्थाय रथमर्जुनमभ्ययात्।
दिव्यं रथं धनुश्‍चैव कृष्णबुद्ध्याऽर्जुनो हरेत् ॥ २६/१६५॥
इति भीतस्तु तां शक्तिमादायार्जुनमृत्यवे।
युद्धायायाद् रथं चापं शक्तिं चैकत्र नाकरोत् ॥ २६/१६६॥
एकं हृतं चेदन्यत् स्यादिति मत्वा भयाकुलः।
बिभेति सर्वदा नीतेः कृष्णस्यामिततेजसः ॥ २६/१६७॥
निश्‍चितो मरणायैव मृतिकाले तु तं रथम्।
आरुह्यागाद्धि पूर्वं तु न कालं मन्यते मृतेः ॥ २६/१६८॥
units.english:
When Karna was uttering filthy words against Bhima, Arjuna attacked him with excellent arrows. Being troubled by Partha’s arrows, Karna ran away from there, having lost his kavacha. Bhima climbed his chariot.

Since Karna had informed Kunti that he would not hurl the Shakti weapon against anyone but Arjuna, he did not use the weapon given by Indra against Bhima. Even through that Shakti, Bhima was always indestructible.

Even when the Narayana-astra fell on his head and remained there for a long time, it did not burn even his hair. What then could Indra’s Shakti do to him? Similarly, what could other great astras and weapons do to him? Note: The episode involving the Narayana astra will be narrated subsequently in this adhyaya.

Knowing Sri Krishna’s sankalpa that the Shakti should become the reason for Ghatotkacha’s death, Bhima did not desire to pick it up even when he had climbed Karna’s chariot.

Later Karna climbed another chariot and went after Arjuna. Due to Sri Krishna’s control of his mind, he feared Arjuna would take away his divine chariot and bows and hence brought with him only the Shakti weapon, to battle and kill Arjuna. He would never bring the (divine) chariot, bow and Shakti weapon together. His thinking was that even if one of them was taken away, he would still possess the others. Due to the strategy of Sri Krishna, the one with unlimited radiance, he always remained in fear.

At the time of his death, he had decided to die and hence he climbed that chariot. Before that, he knew that his time of death had not yet arrived.

units.sanskrit:
शक्तिं तु तद्रथगतां प्रसमीक्ष्य कृष्णः संस्थाप्य पार्थमपि सात्यकिमेव योद्धुम्।
दत्त्वा स्वकीयरथमेव विरोचनस्य पुत्रेण सोऽदिशदमुष्य बलं प्रदाय ॥ २६/१६९॥
शिष्यं त्वशक्तमिह मे प्रतियोधनाय पार्थो ह्यदादिति स सात्यकिमीक्षमाणः।
संस्पर्धयैव युयुधे विरथं चकार तेनैव सात्यकिरमुं हरियानसंस्थः ॥ २६/१७०॥
न केशवरथे कश्‍चित् स्थितो याति पराजयम्।
अतश्‍च सात्यकिर्नाप कर्णेनात्र पराजयम् ॥ २६/१७१॥
शस्त्रसङ्ग्रहकाले तु कुमाराणां व्रतं भवेत्।
इत्युक्तं जामदग्न्येन धनुर्विद्यापुराकृता ॥ २६/१७२॥
तच्छत्रुवधरूपं च पूर्वासिद्धं च गूहितम्।
अविरुद्धं च धर्मस्य कार्यं रामस्य तुष्टिदम् ॥ २६/१७३॥
अनुपद्रवं च लोकस्येत्यतो भीमो व्रतं त्विदम्।
चकार तूबरेत्युक्ते हन्यामिति रहः प्रभुः ॥ २६/१७४॥
अनुपद्रवाय लोकस्य सुव्यक्तश्मश्रुमण्डलः।
सुश्मश्रुं मां न कश्‍चिद्धि तथा ब्रूयादिति स्फुटम् ॥ २६/१७५॥
तदर्जुनो विजानाति स्नेहाद् भीमोदितं रहः।
अर्जुनस्यापि गाण्डीवं देहीत्युक्तो निहन्मि तम् ॥ २६/१७६॥
units.english:
Noticing the presence of the Shakti in his chariot, Sri Krishna stopped Arjuna and, after granting him his own chariot and the necessary strength, ordered Satyaki to fight Karna.

“Arjuna has sent his incapable student to fight me” – interpreting thus, Karna fought Satyaki in battle with a sense of competition. Satyaki, who was riding Sri Krishna’s chariot, in turn rendered Karna chariot-less.

No one seated in Sri Krishna’s chariot could get defeated. Hence Satyaki was not defeated by Karna then.

Sri Parashurama, who had established the art of archery, had established a rule that princes must undertake a vrata at the time of learning weapons.

Such a vrata must facilitate the destruction of enemies. It must be something not done by others, secretive, unopposed to Dharma, pleasing to Sri Parashurama and not against the welfare of the world. Therefore Lord Bhima had undertaken a secret vrata that he would kill anyone who would call him toobara. Note: The word toobara means a person who hasn’t developed beard or a moustache. It was used as an insult in those days.

Knowing that it would never cause harm to the world, Bhima thought no one would call him a toobara since he had a lush beard and moustache and thus undertaken that vow. He had once mentioned the same to Arjuna out of affection, when they were alone.

units.sanskrit:
गाण्डीवस्यागमं पूर्वं जानात्येव हि नारदात्।
इति तच्च विजानाति भीम एको नचापरः ॥ २६/१७७॥
प्रतिज्ञां भीमसेनस्य ब्रुवतः फल्गुने रहः।
दुर्योधनस्तु शुश्राव तां च कर्णाय सोऽब्रवीत् ॥ २६/१७८॥
अतूबरोऽपि तेनासौ तस्मात् तूबर इत्यलम्।
उक्तः प्रकोपनायैव तस्मादर्जुनमब्रवीत् ॥ २६/१७९॥
जानासि मत्प्रतिज्ञां त्वं त्वत्प्रतिज्ञामहं तथा।
अतो हन्तव्यतां प्राप्तो मम वैकर्तनोऽत्र हि ॥ २६/१८०॥
प्रतिज्ञातो वधश्‍चास्य त्वयाऽपि मदनुज्ञया।
अतस्त्वया मयैवायं हन्तव्यः सूतनन्दनः ॥ २६/१८१॥
इत्युक्तो वासविः प्राह हन्तव्योऽयं मयैव हि।
त्वदीयोऽहं यतस्तेन मत्कृतं त्वत्कृतं भवेत् ॥ २६/१८२॥
न त्वत्कृतं मत्कृतं स्याद् गुरुर्मम यतो भवान्।
अतो मयैव हन्तव्य इत्युक्त्वा कर्णमब्रवीत् ॥ २६/१८३॥
रूक्षा वाचः श्रावितोऽयं भीमः कृष्णस्य शृण्वतः।
यच्चाभिमन्युर्युष्माभिरेकः सम्भूय पातितः ॥ २६/१८४॥
units.english:
Arjuna’s vow was to kill anyone who would ask him to hand over the Gandiva to someone else. He had learnt in advance from Sage Narada that he would get the Gandiva. Apart from Bhima, none else knew about it (the secret vow).

When Bhima was mentioning his secret vow to Arjuna, Duryodhana had overheard it and he had informed Karna of the same.

When Karna called him a toobara to enrage him, even when he was not, Bhima told Arjuna thus.

“You are aware of my vow. Similarly, I too know about your oath. Karna has now become fit for killing by me. As per my directions, an oath about his killing has been taken by you too. Therefore, right now, either of us has to kill him”.

When Bhima spoke thus, Arjuna requested – “I shall kill him. Since I am yours, me doing this is equivalent to you doing it as well”. Note: The younger brother fulfilling an oath is equivalent to an older one doing it, as per Shastras. The phrase “I am yours” (tvadeeyaH ahaM) means “I am your family, your younger one”.

“However, what you perform does not count as done by me. Aren’t you the elder one? Therefore it shall be me who will kill him” – saying thus he then addressed Karna.

“Even as Sri Krishna was listening, you have used filthy words against Bhima. Similarly, all of you got together and killed Abhimanyu, who was alone”.

units.sanskrit:
अतस्त्वां निहनिष्यामि त्वत्पुत्रं च तवाग्रतः।

इत्युक्तोऽन्यरथं प्राप्य कर्ण आवीज्जयद्रथम् ॥ २६/१८५॥
द्रौणिकर्णाभिगुप्तं तं नाशकद्धन्तुमर्जुनः।
तत्र वेगं परं चक्रे द्रौणिः पार्थनिवारणे ॥ २६/१८६॥
नचैनमशकत् तर्तुं यत्नवानपि फल्गुनः।
तयोरासीच्चिरं युद्धं चित्रं लघु च सुष्ठु च ॥ २६/१८७॥
तद् दृष्ट्वा भगवान् कृष्णो लोहितायति भास्करे।

अजिते द्रोणतनये त्वहते च जयद्रथे।
अर्जुनस्य जयाकाङ्क्षी ससर्ज तम ऊर्जितम् ॥ २६/१८८॥
तमोव्याप्ते गगने सूर्यमस्तं गतं मत्वा द्रौणिपूर्वाः समस्ताः।
विशश्रमुः सैन्धवश्‍चार्जुनस्य हतप्रतिज्ञस्य मुखं समैक्षत ॥ २६/१८९॥
तदा हरेराज्ञया शक्रसूनुश्‍चकर्त बाणेन जयद्रथस्य।
वह्निं विविक्षन्निव दर्शितः शिरस्तदा वचः प्राह जनार्दनस्तम् ॥ २६/१९०॥
नैतच्छिरः पातय भूतले त्वमितीरितः पाशुपतास्त्रतेजसा।
दधार बाणैरनुपुङ्खपुङ्खैः पुनस्तमूचे गरुडध्वजो वचः ॥ २६/१९१॥
इदं पितुस्तस्य करे निपात्यतां वरोऽस्य दत्तो हि पुराऽमुनाऽयम्।
शिरो निकृत्तं भुवि पातयेद् यस्तवास्य भूयाच्च शिरः सहस्रधा ॥ २६/१९२॥
units.english:
“Therefore I shall kill you. I shall also kill your son in front of you” – when Arjuna spoke thus, Karna climbed another chariot and proceeded to protect Jayadratha.

Arjuna could not kill Jayadratha who was being protected by Ashwathama and Karna. Ashwathama then increased his efforts to stop Arjuna.

In spite of a lot of effort, Arjuna could not get past Ashwathama. An exciting, contained, duel took place between them for a long time.

Bhagavan Sri Krishna noticed it. He saw the Sun turn red. Ashwathama did not look like losing. Jayadratha’s slaying was not yet done. Therefore, desiring victory for Arjuna, Sri Krishna created deep darkness.

When the entire sky was engulfed with darkness, all of them including Drona thought that the Sun had set and relaxed. Saindhava too considered Arjuna as having failed in his vow and approached him to see his (defeated) face.

Then, as per Sri Krishna’s orders, the son of Indra acted as if he was about to enter a fire (to give up his life) and cut off Jayadratha’s head with an arrow. Sri Krishna then told him.

“Do not allow his head to fall on the ground” – when Sri Krishna said thus, Arjuna, using the power of the Pashupatastra, created a stream of arrows back to back and held the head in the sky. Sri Garudadhwaja again said.

“Make this fall on his father’s hands. He has previously given him a boon – ‘Whosoever causes your decapitated head to fall on the ground will have his own head broken into a thousand pieces'” Note: Jayadratha’s father’s name was Vruddhakshatra.

units.sanskrit:
इति स्म वध्योऽस्य पिताऽपि तेनेत्युदीरिते तस्य सन्ध्याक्रियस्य।
अङ्के व्यधात् तच्छिर आशु वासविः स सम्भ्रमात् तद् भुवि च न्यपातयत् ॥ २६/१९३॥
ततोऽभवत् तस्य शिरः सहस्रधा हरिश्‍च चक्रे तमसो लयं पुनः।
तदैव सूर्ये सकलैश्‍च दृष्टे हाहेति वादः सुमहानथासीत् ॥ २६/१९४॥
भीमस्तदा शल्यदुर्योधनादीन् कृपं च जित्वा व्यनदत् सुभैरवम्।
कुर्वन् साहाय्यं फल्गुनस्यैव तुष्टो बभूव शैनेय उतो हते रिपौ ॥ २६/१९५॥
अपूरयत् पाञ्चजन्यं च कृष्णो मुदा तदा देवदत्तं च पार्थः।
भीमस्य नादं सहपाञ्चजन्यघोषं श्रुत्वा निहतं सिन्धुराजम्।
ज्ञात्वा राजा धर्मसुतो मुमोद दुर्योधनश्‍चास सुदुःखितस्तदा ॥ २६/१९६॥
ततो द्रौणिमुखां सेनां सर्वां भीमोऽभ्यवर्तत।
पार्थः कर्णमुखां शिष्टां ततोऽभज्यत तद् बलम् ॥ २६/१९७॥
शीर्णां सेनां प्रविविशुर्धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः।
ततस्तं देशमापुस्ते यत्र भीमधनञ्जयौ ॥ २६/१९८॥
तत एकीकृताः सर्वे पाण्डवाः सहसोमकाः।
परान् विद्रावयामासुस्ते भीताः प्राद्रवन् दिशः ॥ २६/१९९॥
विद्राव्यमाणं सैन्यं तं दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो नृपः।
जयद्रथवधाच्चैव कुपितोऽभ्यद्रवत् परान् ॥ २६/२००॥
units.english:
“Therefore it is required to kill his father as well” – when Sri Krishna said thus, Arjuna immediately made Jayadratha’s head fall on the lap of his father who was doing his sandhyavandana. Out of shock, he threw the head on the ground.

His (Vruddhakshatra’s) head burst into a thousand pieces. Sri Krishna then destroyed the darkness. When the Sun again became visible to all, there was a huge commotion in the Kaurava army.

Bhimasena then defeated Shalya, Duryodhana, Krupa and the others and let out a huge roar in order to assist Arjuna. Satyaki became extremely pleased with Jayadratha’s death.

Sri Krishna blew the Panchajanya. With great joy, Arjuna blew his Devadatta. Hearing the sounds of the Panchajanya along with the roar of Bhima, Dharmaraja gathered Jayadratha had been slain and became very pleased. Duryodhana experienced great sorrow.

Then Bhimasena faced the army that was commandeered by Ashwathama. Arjuna took on the remaining army that was being led by Karna. After that, the armies of Ashwathama and Karna lost.

Dhrishtadyumna and the others entered the midst of that scattered army. They arrived at the place where Bhima and Arjuna were present.

The Pandavas and Panchalas, having been united, started chasing away the enemies. Overcome by fear, they (Kauravas) started running in all directions.

Seeing his army being chased away in that fashion, Duryodhana, angered due to Jayadratha’s killing, pounced on the enemies.

units.sanskrit:
स भीमसेनं च धनञ्जयं च युधिष्ठिरं माद्रवतीसुतौ च।
धृष्टद्युम्नं सात्यकिं द्रौपदेयान् सर्वानेकः शरवर्षैर्ववर्ष ॥ २६/२०१॥
तं विव्यधुस्ते बहुभिः शिलीमुखैः स ताननादृत्य चकर्त बाणैः।
धनूंषि चित्राणि महारथानां चकार सङ्ख्ये विरथौ यमौ च ॥ २६/२०२॥
आदाय चापानि पराणि तेऽपि दुर्योधनं ववृषुः सायकौघैः।
अचिन्तयित्वैव शरान् स एको न्यवारयत् तानखिलांश्‍च बाणैः ॥ २६/२०३॥
तं गाहमानं द्विषतां बहूनां मध्ये द्रोणद्रौणिकृपप्रधानाः।
दृष्ट्वा सर्वे जुगुपुः स्वात्तचापा अनारतं बाणगणान् सृजन्तः ॥ २६/२०४॥
सुयोधनः कर्णमाह जहि भीममिमं युधि।
स आह नैष शक्यो हि जेतुं देवैः सवासवैः ॥ २६/२०५॥
दैवाज्जीवाम्यहं राजन् युद्ध्यंस्तेनातिपीडितः।
अतो घटामहे शक्त्या जयो दैवसमाहितः ॥ २६/२०६॥
दुर्योधनो द्रोणमाह सैन्धवस्त्वदुपेक्षया।
पार्थेन निहतो भीमसात्यकिभ्यां च मे बलम् ॥ २६/२०७॥
प्रतिज्ञा च परित्यक्ता पाण्डवस्नेहतस्त्वया।

इत्युक्तः कुपितो द्रोणः प्रतिज्ञामकरोत् ततः ॥ २६/२०८॥
units.english:
Showering Bhimasena, Dhananjaya, Yudhishthira, the sons of Madri, Dhristhadyumna, Satyaki and the sons of Draupadi with clusters of arrows, he faced them all alone.

They hit back at him with many arrows. Discounting that attack, he cut off a number of different types of bows belonging to many of those great warriors. He rendered Nakula-Sahadeva chariot-less.

All of them picked up different bows and rained a shower of arrows on Duryodhana. Disregarding all of those, he stopped them alone with arrows of his own.

Seeing Duryodhana stuck in the midst of numerous enemies, Drona, Ashwathama, Krupa and the others picked up their bows and started protecting him with relentless arrows.

Duryodhana said to Karna – “Kill this Bhima in battle”. Karna replied – “It is not possible even for Indra and the other Devatas to win against him”.

“O King! Having been tormented by him, it is divine grace that I am still alive. Therefore let us try till our strength allows. Victory is left to providence”.

Duryodhana then condemned Drona – “Due to your neglect Saindhava was killed by Arjuna. My army has been destroyed by Bhima and Satyaki”.

“Out of love for the Pandavas, you have forsaken your vow” – when Duryodhana said thus, Drona got angry and once again made a vow.

units.sanskrit:
इतः परं नैव रणाद् रात्रावहनि वा क्वचित्।
गच्छेयं नच मोक्ष्यामि वर्म बद्धं कथञ्चन ॥ २६/२०९॥
मत्पुत्रश्‍च त्वया वाच्यः पाञ्चालान् नैव शेषय।
सदौहित्रानिति प्रोक्त्वा विजगाहे निशागमे ॥ २६/२१०॥
चमूं परेषामभ्यागाद् धृष्टद्युम्नस्तमाशु च।
द्रौणिदुर्योधनौ तत्र विरथीकृत्य मारुतिः ॥ २६/२११॥
द्रावयामास तत् सैन्यं पश्यतां सर्वभूभृताम्।

अक्षौहिण्यस्तु सप्तैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि ॥ २६/२१२॥
हतास्तासां च भीमेन तिस्रो द्वे फल्गुनेन च।
सौभद्रसात्यकिमुखैस्तन्मध्ये षोडशांशकः ॥ २६/२१३॥
हैडिम्बपार्षतमुखैस्त्रयाच्च दशमांशकः।
भीष्मद्रोणद्रौणिभिश्‍च द्वे समं निहते तदा ॥ २६/२१४॥
तदन्यैर्मिलितैः सर्वैस्तच्चतुर्थांश एव च।
ततो रात्रौ पञ्चभिश्‍च पार्थाः षडि्‌भश्‍च कौरवाः ॥ २६/२१५॥
अक्षौहिणीभिः संव्यूह्य युद्धं चक्रुः सुदारुणम्।

भीमं सेनां द्रावयन्तं पुनः कर्णः समासदत् ॥ २६/२१६॥
units.english:
“From now on, I shall not return from battle, be it night or day. I shall not remove my kavacha under any circumstances”.

“You should inform my son thus – ‘Do not spare any Panchala, including the grandsons from the daughter’s side'” – saying thus, Drona burst into the Pandava army even as nightfall occurred. Note: Drona instructed Ashwathama to kill Draupadi’s sons as well. Draupadi’s sons were ‘dauhitra’ for the Panchala King Drupada.

When he entered the enemy formation thus, Dhrishtadyumna immediately took him on. At the same time, Bhimasena rendered Ashwathama and Duryodhana chariot-less. Having done so, he chased them away, even as all the Kings were watching.

By that time, seven akshouhinis had been killed in both the armies (together). Out of those Bhima had destroyed three and Arjuna had destroyed two. Note: By the evening of day 14, 7 out of the total of 18 akshouhinis had been killed.

Abhimanyu, Satyaki and the others had destroyed one sixteenth out of five akshouhinis. Ghatotkacha, Dhrishtadyumna and the others had destroyed one tenth out of three akshouhinis.

Bhishma, Drona and Ashwathama had killed two akshouhinis of the Pandava army. The rest of them had killed a quarter of that number.

Later that night, the Pandavas with their army of five akshouhinis and the Kauravas with their army of six akshouhinis formed their own vyuhas and engaged in the most terrible battle.

Karna went against Bhima who was scattering away his army. In front of Karna himself, Bhima squashed Dushkarna and Karna, two brothers of Duryodhana, with his foot. The two of them vanished along with their chariots, horses, masts and charioteers. Note: Duryodhana had a brother who too was named Karna.

units.sanskrit:
स कर्णपुरतो भीमो दुष्कर्णं कर्णमेव च।
दुर्योधनस्यावरजौ निष्पिपेष पदा क्षणात् ॥ २६/२१७॥
रथाश्‍वध्वजसूतैश्‍च सहितौ न व्यपश्यताम्।
निरायुधोऽहमिति मां त्वमात्थ परुषं वचः ॥ २६/२१८॥
निरायुधः पदैवाहं त्वां हन्तुमशकं तदा।
इति कर्णस्य तौ भीमः सञ्ज्ञया ज्ञापयन् भुवि ॥ २६/२१९॥
पदा पिपेष कालिङ्गं मुष्टिनैव जघान ह।
मुष्टिना त्वद्वधायाहं समर्थ इति किं वदे ॥ २६/२२०॥
तस्मान्मया रक्षितस्त्वमिति ज्ञापयितुं प्रभुः।
साश्‍वसूतध्वजरथः कालिङ्गो मुष्टिचूर्णितः ॥ २६/२२१॥
केतुमांश्‍च पिता तस्य शक्रदेवः श्रुतायुधः।
अक्षौहिण्या सेनया च सह भीमेन पातिताः ॥ २६/२२२॥
खड्गयुद्धे पुरा भीष्मे सेनापत्यं प्रकुर्वति।
कर्णानुजान् ध्रुवाद्यांश्‍च बहून् जघ्ने स वै निशि ॥ २६/२२३॥
सञ्ज्ञां भीमकृतां ज्ञात्वा शक्तिं चिक्षेप चापराम्।
कर्णः शक्तिर्मया दिव्या न मुक्ता तेन जीवसि ॥ २६/२२४॥
units.english:
“You had rudely called him as empty-handed then. I was fully capable of killing you with my feet even without any weapons”. In order to give such an indication to Karna, Bhima killed the two of them with just his feet. He killed Kalinga with his fist.

“Should I state separately that I can kill you with just my fist too? Still, I have spared you” – in order to indicate to him thus, the omnipotent Bhima crushed Kalinga with this fist, along with his horses, charioteer, mast and chariot.

When Bhishma was the commander, Bhima had killed Ketuman, the father of Kalinga, in a sword fight, along with Shakradeva, Shrutayudha and an entire akshouhini army. Note: In order to revenge the death of his father Ketuman, Kalinga had attacked Bhima. But he too was killed.

In that night, Bhima killed many brothers of Karna including Dhruva. Understanding the signal given by Bhima, Karna hurled another Shakti weapon at him. Note: This was not the Shakti given by Indra to Karna but another one.

units.sanskrit:
इति ज्ञापयितुं तां तु ज्ञात्वा भीमः क्षणात् तदा।
खमुत्पत्य गृहीत्वा च कर्णे चिक्षेप सत्वरः ॥ २६/२२५॥
यदि त्वया तदा मुक्ता शक्तिस्त्वां सा हनिष्यति।
इति ज्ञापयितुं सा च कर्णरक्षणकाङ्क्षिणा ॥ २६/२२६॥
मुक्ता दक्षभुजे साऽथ विदार्य धरणीं तथा।
भित्त्वा विवेश कर्णस्य दर्शयन्ती निदर्शनम् ॥ २६/२२७॥
ततो भीमः पुनः स्वं तु रथमास्थाय चापभृत्।
कर्णस्य पुरतः शत्रून् द्रावयामास सर्वतः ॥ २६/२२८॥
तं कर्णो वारयामास शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः।
भीमः कर्णरथायैव गदां चिक्षेप वेगतः ॥ २६/२२९॥
स तद्गदाविघाताय स्थूणाकर्णास्त्रमासृजत्।
तेनास्त्रेण प्रतिहता सा गदा भीममाव्रजत् ॥ २६/२३०॥
भीमो गदां समादाय कर्णस्य रथमारुहत्।
तया सञ्चूर्णयामास कर्णस्य रथकूबरम् ॥ २६/२३१॥
एवं त्वच्चूर्णने शक्तो मत्कामात् त्वं हि जीवसि।
एवं निदर्शयित्वैव पुनः स्वं रथमाव्रजत् ॥ २६/२३२॥
units.english:
In order to tell Bhima – “I did not exercise the (Indra given) Shakti. Therefore you are still alive” – Karna did thus. Realizing this, Bhima jumped instantly to the sky, held the Shakti with his hand and hurled it back at Karna at great speed.

“If you had used the Shakti back then, it would have killed you” – Bhima conveyed this message in return. Since he wanted to spare Karna, he threw the Shakti at Karna’s right shoulder. That Shakti pierced his shoulder and then pierced the ground and entered it. It delivered a message to Karna as well.

Later Bhima returned to his chariot, picked up his bow and started scattering the enemies in all directions, right in front of Karna!

Karna then tried to stop Bhima by hurling arrows having sharp and bent edges. Bhima threw his mace at Karna’s chariot with great speed.

In order to hit Bhima’s mace, Karna invoked the Sthunakarna astra. The mace, being hit by that astra, returned to Bhima.

Bhima then picked up that mace and climbed Karna’s chariot. He smashed the chariot’s yoke into pieces.

“I can kill you too in this manner. However, I am deliberately sparing you” – conveying such a message through that act, he returned to his chariot.

units.sanskrit:
पुनः कर्णपुरः सेनां जघान बहुशो रणे।

कर्णस्तु तं परित्यज्य सहदेवमुपाद्रवत् ॥ २६/२३३॥
स तु तं विरथीकृत्य धनुः कण्ठेऽवसज्य च।
कुत्सयामास बहुशः स तु निर्वेदमागमत् ॥ २६/२३४॥
न हन्तुमैच्छत् तं कर्णः पृथायै स्वं वचः स्मरन्।
तं विसृज्य रणे कर्णो जघ्ने पार्थवरूथिनीम् ॥ २६/२३५॥
ततो द्रौणिर्विविधैर्बाणसङ्घैर्जघान पार्थस्य चमूं समन्ततः।
सा हन्यमाना रणकोविदेन नाशं लेभे मृत्युनाऽर्ता प्रजेव ॥ २६/२३६॥
दृष्ट्वा सेनां द्रौणिबलाभिभूतां तमाह्वयामास घटोत्कचो युधे।
द्रौणिस्तमाहालमलं न वत्स पुत्रस्तातं योधयस्वाद्य मां त्वम् ॥ २६/२३७॥
इत्युक्त ऊचे न पिता मम त्वं सखा पितुर्यद्यपि शत्रुसंश्रयात्।
अरिश्‍च मेऽसीति तमाह यद्यरिं मां मन्यसे तद्वदहं करोमि ते ॥ २६/२३८॥
इत्यूचिवाञ्छक्रधनुःप्रकाशं विष्फार्य चापं प्रकिरञ्छरौघान्।
अभ्यागमद् राक्षसमुग्रवेगः स्वसेनया सोऽपि तमभ्यवर्तत ॥ २६/२३९॥
स रक्षसां लक्षसमावृतो बली नृभिश्‍च वीरैर्बहुभिः सुशिक्षितैः।
अक्षौहिणीमात्रबलेन राक्षसः सङ्क्षोभयामास गुरोः सुतं शरैः ॥ २६/२४०॥
units.english:
Once again, in front of Karna, Bhima started to kill numerous soldiers. Karna left him and proceeded towards Sahadeva.

Rendering him chariot-less, Karna held Sahadeva’s neck with his bow and insulted him a lot. Sahadeva became very depressed.

Reminding himself of the promise to Kunti, Karna did not wish to kill Sahadeva. Defeating him in battle, he started killing the Pandava army.

Ashwathama then started killing Arjuna’s army from all directions using many varieties of arrows. Being hit by that expert in warfare, the army could not find any respite like a fly on the verge of death.

Noticing the army being destroyed in this manner by Ashwathama’s strength, Ghatotkacha invited him to battle. Ashwathama then said – “O Son! No. No. Being son-like, do not face me now”.

When Ashwathama said thus, Ghatotkacha replied – “You are not father-like to me. However, it is true that you are a friend of my father. But you are my enemy (now) since you have joined the enemy’s camp”. Ashwathama then said – “If you consider me as your enemy then I shall surely behave like one”.

Speaking thus, Ashwathama strung his bow that was radiant like Indra’s bow and rushed against Ghatotkacha at a frightening speed, flooding him with arrows. Ghatotkacha faced him with his army.

The powerful Ghatotkacha, together with a lakh Rakshasas and many brave men, along with an army of one akshouhini, tormented Ashwathama, the Guru’s son, with arrows.

units.sanskrit:
स तेन बाणैर्बहुभिः सुपीडितो विभिन्नगात्रः क्षतजाभिप्लुताङ्गः।
व्यावृत्य नेत्रे कुपितो महद् धनुर्विष्फार्य बाणै रजनीं चकार ॥ २६/२४१॥
सोऽक्षौहिणीं तां क्षणमात्रतः क्षरन् महाशरांस्तानपि राक्षसान् क्षयम्।
निनाय पुत्रं च घटोत्कचस्य निष्ठ्यं पुरा योऽञ्जनवर्मनामकः ॥ २६/२४२॥
निरीक्ष्य सेनां स्वसुतं च पातितं घटोत्कचो द्रोणसुतं शरेण।
विव्याध गाढं स तु विह्वलो ध्वजं समाश्रितश्‍चाशु ससञ्ज्ञकोऽभवत् ॥ २६/२४३॥
उत्थाय बाणं यमदण्डकल्पं सन्धाय चापे प्रविकृष्य राक्षसे।
मुमोच तेनाभिहतः पपात विनष्टसञ्ज्ञः स्वरथे घटोत्कचः ॥ २६/२४४॥
विमूर्च्छितं सारथिरस्य दूरं निनाय युद्धाज्जगतो विपश्यतः।

द्रौणिश्‍च सेनां निशि तैः शरोत्तमैर्व्यद्रावयत् पाण्डवसोमकानाम् ॥ २६/२४५॥
सञ्ज्ञामवाप्याथ घटोत्कचोऽपि क्रुद्धोऽविशत् कौरवसैन्यमाशु।
विद्रावयामास च बाणवर्षैः प्रकम्पयामास महारथांस्तथा ॥ २६/२४६॥
तदैव पार्थं प्रति योद्धुमागतं वैकर्तनं वीक्ष्य जगत्पतिर्हरिः।
घटोत्कचं प्राहिणोच्छक्तिमुग्रां तस्मिन् मोक्तुं पार्थरक्षार्थमेव ॥ २६/२४७॥
स कर्णमाहूय युयोध तेन तस्यानु दुर्योधनपूर्वकाश्‍च ये।
द्रोणेन चैतान् समरे स एको निवारयामास ममर्द चाधिकम् ॥ २६/२४८॥
units.english:
Having been troubled greatly by Ghatotkacha’s numerous arrows, Ashwathama was hurt all over his body. He started bleeding everywhere. Rolling his eyes out of anger, he pulled his great bow and caused darkness with his arrows. Note: Ashwathama fired so many arrows into the sky that it caused darkness in the battlefield.

Firing large arrows in an instant, Ashwathama decimated the akshouhini sized army and all the Rakshasas. He also killed Ghatotkacha’s son called Nishtya. Earlier, Nishtya was known as Anjanavarma. Note: In some recensions of the Mahabharata, Nishtya is known as Anjanavarma. Six generations had participated in the war. Anjanavarma belonged to the last generation.

Seeing his army, along with his son, being killed, Ghatotkacha hit Ashwathama very deeply with an arrow. Hurt badly by that, Ashwathama rested against the flag(pole). He recovered very soon.

Getting up, Ashwathama fixed an arrow that was like Yama’s danda into his bow and, pulling it greatly, released it at the Rakshasa. Ghatotkacha, hit badly by that arrow, fell down unconscious in his chariot.

Even as everyone was watching, his charioteer carried away the deeply unconscious Ghatotkacha far away from battle. Ashwathama started scattering the Pandava and Panchala armies with excellent sharp arrows.

Having regained his consciousness, Ghatotkacha became furious and immediately entered the Kaurava formation. With a shower of arrows he chased them away. He shook many great warriors too.

Noticing Karna arriving to battle with Arjuna, Sri Krishna, the lord of the world, then sent Ghatotkacha. His intention was to get the Shakti thrown against him in order to protect Partha.

Ghatotkacha invited Karna and engaged with him in a duel. He also fought against Duryodhana, Drona and the others who had come with him (Karna) and stopped them single-handedly and troubled them excessively. Note: Rakshasas get additional strength when dark. Hence Ghatotkacha had become very powerful on the 14th night.

units.sanskrit:
ते बाध्यमाना बहुशो बलीयसा कर्णं पुरोधाय तमभ्ययोधयन्।
न विव्यथे तत्र रणे स कर्णः स्ववीर्यमास्थाय महास्त्रवेत्ता ॥ २६/२४९॥
निवारयामास गुरोः सुतं तदा भीमस्त्रिगर्ताञ्छतमन्युनन्दनः।
अलम्बको नाम तदैव राक्षसः समासदत् भीमसुतं निहन्तुम् ॥ २६/२५०॥
युद्ध्वा प्रगृह्यैनमथो निपात्य घटोत्कचो भूमितलेऽसिनाऽस्य।
उत्कृत्य शीर्षं तु सुयोधनेऽक्षिपद् विषेदुरत्राखिलभूमिपालाः ॥ २६/२५१॥
अलायुधोऽथागमदुग्रवीर्यो नराशनस्तं स घटोत्कचोऽभ्ययात्।
युद्ध्वा मुहूर्तं स तु तेन भूमौ निपात्य तं यज्ञपशुं चकार ॥ २६/२५२॥
अथास्य शिर उत्कृत्य क्रोधाद् दुर्योधनोरसि।
चिक्षेप तेन सम्भ्रान्ताः सर्वे दुर्योधनादयः ॥ २६/२५३॥
घटोत्कचबलख्यात्यै समर्थेनापि यो रणे।
न हतो भीमसेनेन हतेऽस्मिन् भैमसेनिना ॥ २६/२५४॥
सर्वे सञ्चोदयामासुः कर्णं शक्तिविमोक्षणे।
अस्मिन् हते हतं सर्वं किं नः पार्थः करिष्यति ॥ २६/२५५॥
एवं सञ्चोद्यमानः स धार्तराष्ट्रैः पुनःपुनः।
हैडिम्बेनार्द्यमानैस्तु स्वयं च भृशपीडितः।
आदत्त शक्तिं विपुलां पाकशासनसम्मताम् ॥ २६/२५६॥
units.english:
Having been hurt badly by that powerful one, all of them engaged with him, keeping Karna in front. In that battle, the great knower of astras Karna excelled with his abilities and continued fighting without losing hope.

Bhima then stopped Guru-putra Ashwathama while the son of Indra stopped the Samshaptakas. At that time, a Rakshasa by name Alambala rushed at the son of Bhima, wanting to kill him.

Ghatotkacha engaged in battle with him and, after bringing him down on the ground, beheaded him with a sword. He threw the head at Duryodhana. All the Kings (fighting on the Kaurava side) there were greatly dejected.

A Rakshasa called Alayudha then rushed at Ghatotkacha, the terrible and valorous man-eating Rakshasa. Facing him, Ghatotkacha battled him for a muhurtha and then made him a yajna- pashu, felling him on the ground. Note: In a yajna, a pashu or animal is sacrificed. Hence the word yajna-pashu here means Ghatotkacha killed Alayudha.

After that, he cut his head and threw it angrily at Duryodhana’s chest. Duryodhana and the others were bewildered by this.

Alayudha, who had been spared by Bhimasena although being capable of killing him so Ghatotkacha could express his strength, was slain by Bhaimasena. Note: Bhaimasena means the son of Bhimasena.

All of them started requesting Karna to use the Shakti against him. “If he dies then all of them are (effectively) dead. What can Arjuna then do to us?” – they said.

Being repeatedly requested by the Kauravas who were tormented by Ghatotkacha, and because he himself was troubled greatly by him, Karna picked up the eminent Shakti that was agreeable to Indra.

units.sanskrit:
तामम्बरस्थाय घटोत्कचाय शैलोपमायातुलविक्रमाय।
चिक्षेप मृत्यो रसनोपमामलं प्रकाशयन्तीं प्रदिशो दिशश्‍च ॥ २६/२५७॥
निर्भिन्नवक्षाः स तया पपात व्यचूर्णयच्छत्रुबलं हतोऽपि।
तस्मिन् हते जहृषुर्धार्तराष्ट्रा उच्चुक्रुशुर्दुधुवुश्‍चाम्बराणि ॥ २६/२५८॥
तदा ननर्त केशवः समाश्लिषच्च फल्गुनम्।
ननाद शङ्खमाधमज्जहास चोरुनिस्वनः ॥ २६/२५९॥
तमपृच्छद् गुडाकेशः किमेतदिति दुर्मनाः।
हते सुतेऽग्रजेऽस्माकं वीरे किं नन्दसि प्रभो ॥ २६/२६०॥
तमाह भगवान् कृष्णो दिष्ट्या जीवसि फल्गुन।
त्वदर्थं निहिता शक्तिर्विमुक्ताऽस्मिन् हि राक्षसे ॥ २६/२६१॥
ततो युधिष्ठिरो दुःखादमर्षाच्चाभ्यवर्तत।
कर्णं प्रति तमाहाथ कृष्णद्वैपायनः प्रभुः ॥ २६/२६२॥
ययाऽर्जुनो निहन्तव्यस्तयाऽसौ राक्षसो हतः।
तन्मा शुचस्त्वं राजेन्द्र दिष्ट्या जीवति फल्गुनः।
इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ व्यासस्ततो युद्धमवर्तत ॥ २६/२६३॥
भीमार्जुनाभ्यामिह हन्यमाने बले कुरूणामितरैश्‍च पाण्डवैः।
प्रदीपहस्ता अथ योधकाश्‍च सर्वेऽपि निद्रावशगा बभूवुः ॥ २६/२६४॥
units.english:
Karna hurled the Shakti, that was like the tongue of death himself and was shining in all directions, at Ghatotkacha who was like a mountain in the sky and incomparably valorous.

With his chest torn apart by that Shakti, Ghatotkacha started falling down. Even though he was getting killed, he fell upon the enemy soldiers and crushed them. When he died, the Kauravas rejoiced. Jeering loudly, they tore up their clothes (in joy).

Sri Krishna then started dancing. Hugging Arjuna tightly, he blew his conch and let out a leonine roar. He laughed with a loud voice.

A sorrow-filled Gudakesha asked him – “O Lord! When our brave elder son has been killed why are you expressing joy in this manner?”

Bhagavan Sri Krishna replied – “Arjuna! By divine providence, you have been spared. Karna utilized the Shakti preserved for you against the Rakshasa”.

After that Yudhishthira started boiling with anger against Karna due to sorrow (of Ghatotkacha’s death). Then, the omnipotent Sri Vyasa arrived there and said.

“Ghatotkacha has been killed by the Shakti which was supposed to kill Arjuna. Therefore, O King, do not mourn. Due to divine grace Arjuna is alive” – saying thus Sri Vyasa departed. The war continued.

When the Kaurava army was destroyed by Bhima and Arjuna, and the Pandava soldiers were getting killed by the Kauravas, all of them, including those holding lamps and the fighters, came under the influence of sleep.

units.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वैव तानाह धनञ्जयस्तदा स्वप्स्यन्तु यावच्छशिनः प्रकाशः।
इतीरिता आशिषः फल्गुनाय प्रयुज्य सर्वे सुषुपुर्यथास्थिताः ॥ २६/२६५॥
पुनश्‍च चन्द्रेऽभ्युदिते युधे ते समाययुः शस्त्रमहास्त्रवर्षाः।
तत्रायातः सात्यकिं सोमदत्तो भूरिश्‍च ताभ्यां युयुधे स एकः ॥ २६/२६६॥
हतौ च तौ पेततुस्तेन भूमौ बाह्लीक एनं समरे त्वयोधयत्।
स सात्यकिं विरथीकृत्य बाणं वधाय तस्याशु मुमोच वीरः ॥ २६/२६७॥
चिच्छेद तं भीमसेनस्त्रिधैव तस्मै शतघ्नीं प्रजहार बाह्लिकः।
तया हतो विह्वलितो वृकोदरो जघान तं गदया सोऽपतच्च ॥ २६/२६८॥
बाह्लीकः प्रार्थयामास पूर्वं स्नेहपुरःसरम्।
भीम त्वयैव हन्तव्यो रणेऽहं प्रीतिमिच्छता ॥ २६/२६९॥
तदा यशश्‍च धर्मं च लोकं च प्राप्नुयामहम्।
इत्युक्त आह तं भीमो नितरां व्यथितस्तदा ॥ २६/२७०॥
हन्यां नैवान्यथा युद्धे तत् ते शुश्रूषणं भवेत्।
इति तेन हतस्तत्र भीमसेनेन बाह्लिकः ॥ २६/२७१॥
हते बाह्लीके कौरवा भीमसेनमभ्याजग्मुः कर्णसुयोधनाद्याः।
द्रौणिं पुरस्कृत्य गुरुं च पार्षतः सभ्रातृकः सात्यकिना समभ्ययात् ॥ २६/२७२॥
units.english:
Seeing all of them under the sway of sleep, Arjuna said – “All of you sleep till moonrise”. When he said thus they thanked him and slept in whatever condition they were in.

Then, when the moon rose, all of them resumed battle, showering weapons and great astras. Somadatta and Bhuri faced Satyaki. He started fighting the two of them all by himself.

Both of them fell down on the ground, slain by Satyaki. Then, Bahlika faced him in battle. The brave Bahlika rendered Satyaki chariot-less and released an arrow intending to kill him.

Bhimasena cut that arrow released by Bahlika into three pieces. The latter then threw a weapon called Shataghni at Bhima. Bhima acted like he was jolted by it and hit Bahlika with his mace. Bahlika fell down dead.

Bahlika had earlier affectionately requested – “Bhima! You alone should kill me in battle out of love for me. I shall then attain fame, punya and excellent lokas”.

When Bahlika requested thus, Bhima told him – “You should cause me a lot of pain. Only then shall I slay you in battle. I will not do so otherwise. Causing such pain to me will only lead you to attain punya due to your service”. Thus, Bahlika was killed there by Bhimasena.

When Bahlika was killed, Karna, Duryodhana and the other Kaurava heroes rushed against Bhimasena, keeping Ashwathama and Drona at the head. Dhrishtadyumna, joined by his brothers and Satyaki, faced Guru Drona.

units.sanskrit:
संशप्तकैरेव पार्थो युयोध तद् युद्धमासीदतिरौद्रमद्भुतम्।
अक्षौहिणी तत्र भीमार्जुनाभ्यां निषूूदिता रात्रियुद्धे समस्ता ॥ २६/२७३॥
ततः सूर्यश्‍चाभ्युदितस्तदाऽतिघोरं द्रोणः कर्म युद्धे चकार।
स पाञ्चालानां रथवृन्दं प्रविश्य जघान हस्त्यश्‍वरथान् नरांश्‍च ॥ २६/२७४॥
विद्रावितास्तेन महारथाश्‍च नैवाविन्दञ्छर्म बाणान्धकारे।
युवेव वृद्धोऽपि चचार युद्धे स उग्रधन्वा परमास्त्रवेत्ता ॥ २६/२७५॥
रथार्बुदं तेन हतं च तत्र ततः सहस्रं गुणितं नराणाम्।
ततो दशांशो निहतो हयानां गजार्बुदं चैव रणोत्कटेन ॥ २६/२७६॥
तथा विराटद्रुपदौ शराभ्यां निनाय लोकं परमाजिमध्ये।
ततो विजित्यैव गुरोः सुतादीन् धृष्टद्युम्नं भीमसेनो जुगोप ॥ २६/२७७॥
धृष्टद्युम्नो भीमसेनाभिगुप्तो द्रोणं हन्तुं यत्नमुच्चैश्‍चकार।
निवारयामास गुरुः शरौघैर्धृष्टद्युम्नं सोऽपि तं सायकेन।
विव्याध तेनाभिहतः स मूर्च्छामवाप विप्रो निषसाद चाशु ॥ २६/२७८॥
धृष्टद्युम्नः सत्वरं खड्गचर्मणी आदाय तस्यारुरुहे रथोत्तमम्।
सञ्ज्ञामवाप्याथ गुरुः शरौघैः प्रादेशमात्रैर्व्यथयामास तं च ॥ २६/२७९॥
स तैरतिव्यथितस्तद्रथाच्च परावृत्तः स्वरथमारुरोह।
सुसंरब्धौ तौ पुनरेव युद्धं सञ्चक्रतुर्वृष्टशराम्बुधारौ ॥ २६/२८०॥
units.english:
Arjuna engaged in battle with the Samshaptakas. That battle was extremely terrible and amazing. In that battle at night, an army of one akshouhini was killed by Bhima and Arjuna.

Then, the Sun rose. Drona then performed the most dreadful task in the war. Entering the chariot formation of the Panchalas, he killed elephants, horses, chariots (chariot warriors) and foot-soldiers.

Drona caused even great warriors to run away. In that darkness caused by arrows (of Drona), they couldn’t find any peace. Although aged, Drona, the most knowledgeable expert on astras and a terrifying archer, moved around in battle like a youngster.

Twenty thousand chariot-warriors were killed by Drona, the battle-expert! A thousand times more foot-soldiers were killed. Horses numbering a tenth of the soldiers died while twenty thousand elephants too were slain.

Similarly, with two arrows, Drona dispatched Virata and Drupada from the war-world to the other- world. After that, Bhimasena won against Guru-putra Ashwathama and others and engaged in protecting Dhrishtadyumna.

Under the protection of Bhimasena, Dhrishtadyumna tried very hard to kill Drona. With a flood of arrows, Drona stopped Dhrishtadyumna forcefully, who then hit him very hard with an arrow. Drona fell unconscious due to that blow.

Dhrishtadyumna quickly picked up a sword and shield and started climbing the excellent chariot of Drona. By that time, Drona, having regained consciousness, started hurting him with arrows that were yard-long in length.

Pained by those arrows, Dhrishtadyumna returned and climbed his chariot. The two of them tried extremely hard and battled again, raining arrows at each other.

units.sanskrit:
निवार्य शत्रुं स शरैर्ब्रह्मास्त्रमसृजद् द्विजः।
तेन सन्दाहयामास पाञ्चालान् सुबहून् रणे ॥ २६/२८१॥
पुरुजित् कुन्तिभोजश्‍च तेनान्ये च हतास्तदा।

भीमोऽर्जुनः सात्यकिश्‍च पर्यायेण गुरोः सुतम् ॥ २६/२८२॥
दूरतो वारयामासुर्महत्या सेनया सह।
कर्णदुर्योधनादींश्‍च शल्यं भोजं कृपं तथा ॥ २६/२८३॥
भीमार्जुनौ शरौघेण वारयामासतू रणे।
तत्र भीमो गजानीकं जयत्सेनं च मागधम् ॥ २६/२८४॥
जघान सुबहूंश्‍चैव मागधानां रथव्रजान्।

अथ मालवराजस्य त्वश्‍वत्थामाभिधं गजम् ॥ २६/२८५॥
भीमसेनहतं दृष्ट्वा वासुदेवप्रचोदितः।
अश्‍वत्थामा हत इति प्राह राजा युधिष्ठिरः ॥ २६/२८६॥
अश्‍वत्थामवधं श्रुत्वा नाहं योत्स्य इति स्वयम्।
पुरोक्तं धर्मजायैव तेन द्रोणो युधिष्ठिरम् ॥ २६/२८७॥
ब्रूहि सत्यमिति प्राह सत्यमित्येव सोऽब्रवीत्।
उपांशु कुञ्जरश्‍चेति द्रोणोऽतो व्यथितोऽभवत् ॥ २६/२८८॥
units.english:
Drona stopped Dhrishtadyumna with arrows and invoked the Brahmastra and burnt numerous Panchalas in that war. Purujit, Kuntibhoja and others were killed by him then.

One after the other, Bhima, Arjuna and Satyaki stopped Ashwathama and his big army at a distance. Note: By stopping Ashwathama in this manner, they made it possible for Dhrishtadyumna to challenge Drona to try and kill him.

Bhima and Arjuna stopped Karna, Duryodhana and the others, including Shalya, Krutavarma and Krupa in that battle, through a flood of arrows.

Bhima then destroyed an army of elephants and a King of Magadha named Jayatsena. He also destroyed a large contingent of chariots belonging to the Magadhas.

At that time, seeing an elephant named Ashwathama, belonging to the King of Malava, being killed by Bhimasena, King Yudhisthira, provoked by Sri Krishna, said – “Ashwathama is dead”.

Drona himself had earlier told Dharmaraja that he would not be able to continue fighting the war after hearing about Ashwathama’s death. Therefore, he asked Yudhisthira – “Tell me the truth”. Dharmaraja replied – “It is the truth” but added the word “elephant” in an unclear voice. Drona underwent a lot of pain due to that (news). Note: Dharmaraja said “AshwathamO hataH kunjaraH”. The word kunjara was uttered in a very unclear (low) voice by him, which Drona did not hear. Assuming that Dharmaraja was talking about his son, he became dejected.

units.sanskrit:
तस्य भीमो रथेषां च गृहीत्वा न तवेदृशम्।
योग्यं गुणवतो नित्यं परधर्मोपजीवनम् ॥ २६/२८९॥
इत्याह खस्था मुनयश्‍चालमेहीति तं तदा।
ऊचुस्तदखिलं ज्ञात्वा द्रोणः शस्त्रमवासृजत् ॥ २६/२९०॥
सन्यस्य कर्माणि तदाऽखिलानि योगारूढः परमं वासुदेवम्।
सर्वेश्‍वरं नित्यनिरस्तदोषं ध्यायन् मुक्त्वा देहमगात् स्वधाम ॥ २६/२९१॥
तं केशवः पाण्डवा गौतमश्‍च यान्तं स्वलोकं ददृशुर्विहायसा।

धृष्टद्युम्नः पाण्डवैर्वार्यमाणोऽप्यगात् खड्गं चर्म चादाय तत्र ॥ २६/२९२॥
छित्वाऽसिना तस्य शिरः पुनश्‍च रथं स्वकीयं त्वरया समास्थितः।
दृष्ट्वा कृपस्तं सुभृशं भयार्दितः सम्प्राद्रवद् वाजिनमेकमास्थितः ॥ २६/२९३॥
सञ्छिन्ने द्रोणशिरसि गर्हयामास वासविः।
युधिष्ठिरश्च पाञ्चाल्यं सात्यकिश्‍चापि कोपितः ॥ २६/२९४॥
धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु तावाह कथं भूरिश्रवा हतः।
इति तं सात्यकिः क्रुद्धो गदापाणिः समभ्ययात्।
आह्वयामास पाञ्चाल्यस्तं धृतासिरविस्मयः ॥ २६/२९५॥
तदा जग्राह शैनेयं भीमः कृष्णप्रचोदितः।
शमयामास पार्थं च पाञ्चाल्यस्नेहयन्त्रितः ॥ २६/२९६॥
units.english:
Bhima held the pole at the front end of Drona’s chariot and told him – “It doesn’t befit a noble person such as yourself to live doing what is not your natural Dharma”. The sages who had gathered in the skies invited him saying – “It is enough. Come back now”. Realizing all of this, Drona gave up his weapons.

Drona submitted all his Karma performed till then to Sri Vasudeva. Sitting in yoga and meditating on Sri Krishna, the Lord of all, the one who is free from all defects and the best amongst all, Drona gave up his body and returned to his loka.

Sri Krishna, the Pandavas and Krupa saw Drona returning back to his world through the skies. In spite of being stopped by the Pandavas, Dhrishtadyumna picked up his sword and shield and went where Drona was present. Note: Drona had already left the world. Only his body remained, which Dhrishtadyumna approached.

He beheaded him with his sword and quickly climbed his chariot again. Seeing this, Krupa became very scared and, having climbed his horse, ran away quickly from there.

When Dhrishtadyumna cut Drona’s head thus, Arjuna and Yudhisthira condemned him. Satyaki too became very angry.

Dhrishtadyumna asked both of them – “How did you kill Bhurishravas?”. This angered Satyaki a lot and he and attacked him, holding a mace in his hand.

Without getting perturbed, Dhrishtadyumna invited Satyaki for a duel. Bhima then, having been prodded by Sri Krishna, held Satyaki. Bound by his love for Dhrishtadyumna, he got Arjuna to calm down.

units.sanskrit:
ते वासुदेवेन तदा सुुशिक्षिताः स्नेहं पुनः पूर्ववदापुरुत्तमम्।
यत्ताश्‍च युद्धाय समुद्यताश्‍च तदाऽगमद् द्रौणिरप्यात्तधन्वा ॥ २६/२९७॥
आश्रुत्य तातं निहतं प्रतिज्ञां चकार निःशेषरिपुप्रमाथने।
नारायणास्त्रं विससर्ज कोपात् तदा भीता भीममृते समस्ताः ॥ २६/२९८॥
युधिष्ठिरः प्राह विषण्णचेतनः शैनेयपूर्वाः प्रतियान्तु सर्वे।
सभ्रातृकोऽहं द्रौणिवरास्त्रभग्नो भवेयमित्यत्र जगाद केशवः ॥ २६/२९९॥
नमध्वमस्त्रस्य ततो विमोक्ष्यथेत्यथ प्रणेमुश्‍च धनञ्जयादिकाः।
सर्वे न भीमस्तदमुष्य मूर्ध्नि पपात सोऽग्नाविव संस्थितोऽग्निः ॥ २६/३००॥
अदह्यमाने भीमेऽपि वह्नौ वह्निरिव स्थिते।
अवेष्टयद् वारुणेन पार्थोऽत्रात्मप्रपत्तये ॥ २६/३०१॥
न देहे पतितास्त्रस्य बहिर्वेष्टनतः फलम्।
तथाऽपि स्नेहवशगो वेष्टयामास फल्गुनः ॥ २६/३०२॥
अमोघत्वं निजास्त्रस्य भीमस्यावध्यतामपि।
साधयन् सार्जुनः कृष्णो भीमस्य रथमारुहत् ॥ २६/३०३॥
वेष्टितं वारुणास्त्रेण प्रविष्टं बाह्यतस्तदा।
सहितत्वात् केशवेन नरत्वादथ फल्गुनम् ॥ २६/३०४॥
units.english:
After being advised specially by Sri Krishna, all of them became friendly with each other like before. Holding their weapons, they became ready for battle and left. Then, Ashwathama arrived, holding his bow.

Getting to know of his father’s killing, Ashwathama undertook an oath to kill all enemies sparing none. Enraged, he invoked the Narayana astra. Then, except Bhima, all of them became scared.

Yudhishthira, with a heavy heart, said – “Let Satyaki and the others get away from here. I shall fall victim, along with my brothers, to the excellent astra of the son of Drona”. Sri Krishna then replied.

“Bow down to the astra. Then you shall be released from it”. Immediately Arjuna and the others bowed down to it. Bhima did not do so. That astra fell on his head. He stood in the middle of the astra like a fire standing amidst another fire.

When Bhima stood there like a fire that doesn’t get burnt by another fire, Arjuna, in order to show his affection, invoked the Varunastra to protect Bhima.

When an astra falls in that manner on the body, sprinkling water from outside is of no use. Still, bound by his friendship (brotherly love), Arjuna attempted to provide protection through that astra.

Conveying (to everyone) that his astra was unassailable and the fact that Bhima could never be killed, Sri Krishna climbed Bhima’s chariot along with Arjuna. Note: The Narayana astra is Sri Vishnu’s weapon. Hence Sri Krishna is it’s owner.

Because of the cover provided outside by the Varunastra, because of Sri Krishna’s company and because of Nara’s Avesha in him, the Narayana astra did not burn Arjuna. The astra became extinguished as the two of them (Sri Krishna and Arjuna) brought Bhima down from his chariot and took away his weapon.

units.sanskrit:
तदस्त्रं नादहत् ताभ्यां स्वरथादवरोपिते।
भीम आच्छिन्नहेतौ च तदस्त्रं शान्तिमागमत् ॥ २६/३०५॥
शुद्धक्षत्रियधर्मेषु निरतो यद् वृकोदरः।
वाहनादवतीर्यान्यैः प्रणतेऽपि निरायुधैः।
सायुधः सरथी युद्ध्यदविषह्यमपीश्‍वरैः ॥ २६/३०६॥
स्वधर्महानौ मित्राणां कर्तव्यं यन्निषेधनम्।
अतः सोऽन्यानपि प्राह मा नमध्वमिति स्वयम् ॥ २६/३०७॥
नमस्कार्यमपि ह्यस्त्रं न नम्यं जीवनेच्छया।
समरे शत्रुणा मुक्तं तस्मात् तं न चकार सः ॥ २६/३०८॥
अस्त्राभिमानी वायुर्हि देवताऽस्य हरिः स्वयम्।
तस्माद् भीमस्वरूपत्वान्नादहच्चाग्निमग्निवत् ॥ २६/३०९॥
मनसैवादरं चक्रे भीमोऽस्त्रे च हरौ तदा।
क्षत्रधर्मानुसारेण न ननाम च बाह्यतः ॥ २६/३१०॥
वासुदेवः स्वकीयास्त्रं भीमं चामोघमेव तु।
साधयित्वाऽनन्तशक्तिः पुनरश्‍वानचोदयत् ॥ २६/३११॥
पुनः प्रयोक्तुमस्त्रं तद् धार्तराष्ट्रोऽभ्यचोदयत्।
द्रौणिर्न शक्यमित्युक्त्वा धृष्टद्युम्नं समभ्ययात् ॥ २६/३१२॥
units.english:
Vrikodara was the adherent of the pristine Bhagavata Dharma at all times. Hence, even when all others got down from their vehicles and prostrated before the astra, Bhima alone stayed in his chariot holding his weapon and fought that Narayana astra which even the most powerful Devatas could not tolerate.

When the situation is such that one’s Swadharma is about to be harmed, it is duty to advise friends to not violate. Therefore, Bhima asked the others also to not bow down to the astra. Note: Bhima asks all the warriors around him to not bow down to the astra. Since he followed the Bhagavata Dharma it was his duty to encourage his friends to follow the same path too. Hence his advice.

Although the astra is worthy of worship, when it is released by an enemy in war, it is not appropriate to bow to it out of attachment over life. Therefore, Bhima did not bow down to it.

Sri Vayu is the presiding deity of the Narayana astra while Sri Hari himself is the deity propagated by it. Therefore, since the astra was the very essence of Bhima, it did not burn him, just as a fire does not burn another fire. Note: Every divine astra has a abhimani devata or presiding deity. This deity controls the astra. Every such astra also has a pratipadya devata or propagating deity. This is the Devata that is served by the astra.

Bhimasena paid his respects to the astra and its Devata Sri Hari in his mind itself. However, in accordance with Kshatriya Dharma, he did not bend his head externally.

Showing (to everyone) that his astra and Bhima were both unfailing, Sri Krishna, the omnipotent, started driving the horses once again.

Duryodhana pleaded fervently with Ashwathama to invoke the astra once again. Saying that it was not possible, the son of Drona proceeded against Dhrishtadyumna.

units.sanskrit:
आयान्तमीक्ष्यैव गुरोः सुतं तं धृष्टद्युम्नं सात्यकिरन्वयाद् रणे।
उभौ च तौ सायकाभ्यामविध्यन्निपेततुस्तौ च विमूर्च्छितौ रणे ॥ २६/३१३॥
भीमस्याभ्यागतस्याश्‍वान् द्रौणिर्व्यद्रावयद् रणे।
संस्थापयति तान् भीमे ददर्श द्रौणिमर्जुनः ॥ २६/३१४॥
ततोऽर्जुनस्तं प्रतियोद्धुमागमद् रूक्षा वाचः श्रावयन् क्रुद्धरूपः।
तत्राग्नेयं द्रौणिरमुञ्चदस्त्रं तेन व्याप्ता पृतना पाण्डवानाम् ॥ २६/३१५॥
अक्षौहिणी निहता चात्र सेना पार्थं सयानं हरिरुज्जहार।
जीवन्तमालोक्य सुरेन्द्रनन्दनं द्रौणिः कोपात् कार्मुकं चापहाय।
ययौ तमागत्य जगाद कृष्णो वेदान्तकृत् पूर्णषाड्गुण्यदेहः ॥ २६/३१६॥
मा याहि साक्षाद् गिरिशः सुराणां कार्याय भूमौ बलवानजायथाः।
महच्च कार्यं पुनरस्ति दृष्टं तवाशु तच्च प्रतिपादयेति ॥ २६/३१७॥
तथोदितः प्रातरिति ब्रुवाणो ययौ प्रणम्याखिलवेदयोनिम्।
ययुस्तमन्वेव सुयोधनादयो दुःखानतास्ते शिबिराय भीताः ॥ २६/३१८॥
पार्थाश्‍च सर्वे मुदिता जनार्दनं परं स्तुवन्तः शिबिराय जग्मुः।
तत्रापि रात्रावमितान् हरेर्गुणाननुस्मरन्तो मुमुदुः समेताः ॥ २६/३१९॥
॥ इति श्रीमदानन्दतीर्थभगवत्पादाचार्यविरचिते श्रीमन्महाभारततात्पर्यनिर्णये नारायणास्त्रोपशमनं नाम षड्विंशोऽध्यायः॥
units.english:
Seeing the son of Guru (Drona) approaching Dhrishtadyumna, Satyaki too joined the battle. Ashwathama hurt both of them with his arrows. The two of them fell down unconscious.

Ashwathama chased away the horses of Bhima when he arrived there. Even as Bhima controlled the horses, Arjuna saw Ashwathama.

Arjuna then came there to fight Ashwathama. Condemning him with cruel words, Ashwathama invoked the Agneyastra. That astra surrounded the Pandavas from all sides.

One akshouhini sized army was then destroyed (by that astra). Sri Krishna protected Arjuna along with the chariot. Seeing Arjuna escaping alive, Ashwathama threw away his bow in anger and went away.

Sri Vyasa, the one who composed the Brahmasutras and one whose body is verily the six auspicious attributes, arrived there and told him – “Do not leave. You are verily the Avatara of Girisha. To accomplish the task of the Devatas, you, the powerful one, have taken birth on Earth”.

“I know that you need to accomplish a great task in future. Therefore undertake that soon” – when Sri Vyasa said thus Ashwathama said – “In the morning” and bowed to the propagator of the entire Vedas and left. Behind him, Duryodhana and the others too held their heads low out of sorrow and fear and went to their camps.

All the Pandavas, being overjoyed, sang praises of Sri Krishna, the Supreme One, and went to their camps. There too, they remembered the auspicious qualities of Sri Hari at night, and felt great joy together. composed by Srimadanandatirtha Bhagavatpada ||

units.sanskrit:
ॐ॥ अथानुज्ञामुपादाय द्रौणेर्दुर्योधनो नृपः।
कर्णं सेनापतिं चक्रे सोऽगाद् युद्धाय दंशितः ॥ २७/१॥
तत्राभवद् युद्धमतीव दारुणं पाण्डोः सुतानां धृतराष्ट्रजैर्गजे।
तत्रोदयाद्रिप्रतिमे प्रदृश्यते भीमो यथोद्यत्सविताऽतिनिर्मलः ॥ २७/२॥
तं कालयन्तं नृपतीन् क्षेमधूर्तिरभ्यागमत् तस्य गजं जघान च।
तं वीर्यमत्तं प्रतिलभ्य भीमो निनाय मृत्योः सदनाय शीघ्रम् ॥ २७/३॥
निहत्य तं मारुतिरभ्यकृन्तच्छिरांसि यूनां परपक्षपातिनाम्।
विक्षोभयामास च शत्रुसैन्यं सिंहो यथैव श्‍वसृगालयूथम् ॥ २७/४॥
सङ्क्षोभ्यमाणं तदनीकमीक्ष्य द्रौणी रथेन प्रतिजग्मिवांस्तम्।
तद् युद्धमासीदतिघोरमद्भुतं पुरा यथा नास च कस्यचित् क्वचित् ॥ २७/५॥
दृष्ट्वैव तद् देवगन्धर्वविप्रा ऊचुर्नेदृग् दृष्टपूर्वं सुयुद्धम्।
नचोत्तरं वाऽपि भविष्यतीदृक् कलां च सर्वाणि न षोडशीमयुः ॥ २७/६॥
नैतादृशी ज्ञानसम्पद् बलं वा द्वयं कुतो वायुमृते शिवं तथा।
द्वयोः समाहार इह द्वयोरपि ज्ञानस्य बाह्वोश्‍च बलस्य सूर्जितः ॥ २७/७॥
इतीर्यमाणे विबुधैर्नरोत्तमौ दिशः समस्ता गगनं च पत्रिभिः।
निरन्तरं चक्रतुरुत्तमोजसौ दृष्ट्वैव तद् प्रीतिमगुर्महारथाः ॥ २७/८॥
units.english:
Later King Duryodhana took the consent of the son of Drona and appointed Karna as the commander- in-chief. Karna put on his Kavacha and proceeded to battle.

Under the commandership of Karna, an extremely terrible battle took place between the Kauravas and Pandavas. Bhima came to the battlefield appearing like the rising pristine Sun on an elephant that was like the Udayadri mountain. Note: Udayadri mountain – mountain/hill on the eastern side behind which the Sun rises.

Kshemadhoorti approached Bhima as the latter was hurting all the Kings. He killed Bhima’s elephant. Facing that King who had swelled with pride over his strength, Bhima immediately dispatched him to the abode of Yama.

Having killed him, Maruti cut off the heads of the young fighters in the enemy camp. He put the enemy army into great turmoil, just as a lion does to a pack of jackals.

When that army was in such a tumultuous situation, Ashwathama climbed his chariot and faced Bhima. The battle between them was unprecedented, having never taken place between any two warriors before. It was terrifying and amazing.

As soon as they witnessed this battle, the Devatas, Gandharvas and Munis spoke – “We have never seen such a great battle before. Neither will such a duel take place in future. All other battles are not equal to even one sixteenth of this one”.

“Such wealth of knowledge and strength is not present in anyone apart from Vayu and Shiva. Where else can these two get together? The strength of knowledge and prowess – both these have complete presence in these two”.

Even as the Devatas spoke thus, Bhima and Ashwathama, the best amongst men and excellent fighters, filled all directions and the sky with their arrows. The other great warriors in that battlefield became frightened seeing this.

units.sanskrit:
शरासने मारुतिना निराकृते द्रौणिर्महास्त्राणि मुमोच तस्मिन्।
तान्यस्त्रवर्यैर्बलवानविस्मयः संशामयामास सुतोऽनिलस्य ॥ २७/९॥
पुनः शरैरेव परस्परं तावयुद्ध्यतां चित्रमलं च सुष्ठु।
तदा तु भीमस्य शरैर्भृशार्दितो द्रौणिः पपाताशु दृढं विचेतनः ॥ २७/१०॥
भीमश्‍च विह्वलतनुः स तु किञ्चिदेव पूर्वं गते गुरुसुते प्रययौ क्षणेन।
निर्धूतयुद्धश्रम आत्तधन्वा योद्धुं गजौघं प्रति नादिताशः ॥ २७/११॥
तस्मिन् गजान् मर्दयति धार्तराष्ट्रो युधिष्ठिरम्।
अगाद् युद्धाय तौ युद्धं राजानौ चक्रतुश्‍चिरम् ॥ २७/१२॥
तत्र तं विरथं चक्रे सहसैव युधिष्ठिरः।
स गदामाददे गुर्वीं तं भीमोऽभ्यपतद् गदी ॥ २७/१३॥
दृष्ट्वा कृपस्तं स्वरथमारोप्यापययौ ततः।

तदैव कर्णनकुलौ भृशं बाणैरयुद्ध्यताम् ॥ २७/१४॥
नकुलं विरथं कृत्वा कर्णोऽथ प्रपलायिनम्।
अनुद्रुत्य च वेगेन कण्ठे धनुरवासृजत् ॥ २७/१५॥
उक्त्वा च परुषा वाचः कुन्त्या वचनगौरवात्।
न जघानैव नकुलं विसृज्य च ययौ परान् ॥ २७/१६॥
units.english:
When Bhima cut off Ashwathama’s bow, he rained many great astras at Bhima. The son of Vayu, being a powerful one himself, did not get perturbed and extinguished them with great astras of his own.

Once again, the two of them fought each other with arrows in the most amazing manner. Ashwathama then, being hurt badly by Bhima’s arrows, fell deeply unconscious.

As Ashwathama departed from there after being unconscious, Bhimasena, who was only mildly tired, immediately recovered from battle fatigue and picked up his bow. Letting out a leonine roar that echoed from all directions, he proceeded to battle the elephant army.

When Bhimasena was destroying the elephants, Duryodhana went against Yudhishthira in battle. The two Kings fought against each other for a long time.

Yudhishthira quickly ensured Duryodhana was left chariot-less. Duryodhana then picked up a big mace. Bhima picked up his own mace and went after him.

Seeing Bhima, Krupa made Duryodhana climb his chariot and left from there. Thereafter Karna and Nakula started fighting forcefully with arrows.

Karna rendered Nakula chariot-less and, when the latter started running away, chased him speedily and jabbed at his neck with his bow.

Berating him with acerbic words, Karna let go off Nakula out of respect for his promise to Kunti, and went against others.

units.sanskrit:
विन्दानुविन्दावथ कैकयौ रणे समासदत् सात्यकिरुग्रविक्रमः।
तयोरमुष्याभवदुग्रवैशसं प्रवर्षतोरुत्तमसायकान् बहून् ॥ २७/१७॥
ताभ्यां निरुद्धः सहसा जहार तत्रानुविन्दस्य शिरोऽथ विन्दः।
युयोध शैनेयमथारथावुभौ परस्परं चक्रतुरुत्तमाहवे ॥ २७/१८॥
ततश्‍च चर्मासिधरौ प्रचेरतुः श्येनौ यथाऽऽकाशतले कृतश्रमौ।
निकृत्य चान्योन्यमुभौ च चर्मणी वरासिपाणी युगपत् समीयतुः ॥ २७/१९॥
तत्रापहस्तेन शिरः सकुण्डलं जहार विन्दस्य मृधे स सात्यकिः।
निहत्य तौ बन्धुजनैः सुपूजितो जगाम शत्रूनपरान् प्रकम्पयन् ॥ २७/२०॥
कृपमायान्तमीक्ष्यैव तपसा मां प्रपीडयेत्।
इति मत्वा पार्षतस्तु भीमं शरणमेयिवान् ॥ २७/२१॥
कर्णं समन्तात् प्रतिकालयन्तं वरूथिनीमिन्द्रसुतः समभ्ययात्।
क्षणात् तमाजौ विरथं च चक्रे ततोऽपहारं स चकार चम्वाः ॥ २७/२२॥
पराजितः संयति सूर्यसूनुः सुतेन शक्रस्य स धार्तराष्ट्रम्।

जगाद बाहुं प्रतिगृह्य पार्थो जिगाय मामन्यमनस्कमाजौ ॥ २७/२३॥
कामं रथो मे धनुरप्यभेद्यं दत्तं भृगूणामधिपेन दिव्यम्।
यन्ता न तादृङ् मम यादृशो हरिः शल्यो यदि स्यात् त्वदरिं निहन्याम् ॥ २७/२४॥
units.english:
The terrifying fighter Satyaki faced Vinda and Anuvinda. He started raining them with numerous excellent arrows. An intense battle took place between him and the two of them. Note: These two, named Vinda and Anuvinda, were the Kings of Kekaya country.

Being stopped by the two of them, Satyaki quickly decapitated Anuvinda. After that Vinda fought against him. In that excellent battle, the two of them destroyed each other’s chariots.

Later those two experts in warfare held swords and shields in their hands and started fighting, like hawks in the sky. Destroying each other’s shields they held excellent swords in their hands and rushed simultaneously at each other.

Satyaki then, with his hands, caused the head of Vinda that was (decorated) with ear-rings to fly in battle (i.e. decapitated him). Having killed the two of them, he was greatly worshipped by his folks and he proceeded further, causing tremors amongst the enemies.

Dhrishtadyumna saw Krupa approaching him and realized that he could hurt him with his taposhakti and took refuge in Bhima.

Arjuna went against Karna who was slaughtering the soldiers from all sides. He swiftly rendered Karna chariot-less, who then withdrew his army.

Karna, having been defeated by Arjuna, held Duryodhana’s hand and said – “Arjuna defeated me when my mind was elsewhere”.

“Parashurama has given me the chariot and divine indestructible bows that I need. However I do not have a charioteer like Krishna. If Shalya becomes my charioteer then I can kill your enemy”.

units.sanskrit:
इतीरिते सौत्यकृते स शल्यं प्रोवाच स क्रुद्ध इवाभवत् तदा।
दुर्योधनो रथिनः सारथेस्तु व्यावर्णयन्नुत्तमतामशामयत् ॥ २७/२५॥
बुद्ध्या बलेन ज्ञानेन धैर्याद्यैरपि योऽधिकः।
रथिनः सारथिः स स्यादर्जुनस्य यथा हरिः ॥ २७/२६॥
यथा शिवस्य ब्रह्माऽभूद् दहतस्त्रिपुरं पुरा।
इत्यादिवाक्यैः संशान्त इव शल्योऽस्य सारथिः ॥ २७/२७॥
बभूव तेन सहितः सेनां व्यूह्य रवेः सुतः।
गच्छन् युद्धाय दर्पेण प्राह यो मेऽर्जुनं पुमान् ॥ २७/२८॥
दर्शयेत् तस्य दास्यामि प्रीतो वित्तमनर्गलम्।
इति ब्रुवाणं बहुशः प्राह शल्यः प्रहस्य च ॥ २७/२९॥
निवातकवचा येन हता दग्धं च खाण्डवम्।
को नाम तं जयेन्मर्त्यो दृष्टो वाऽपि स गोग्रहे ॥ २७/३०॥
काकगोमायुधर्मा त्वं हंससिंहोपमं रणे।
मा याहि पार्थं मा याहि हतोऽनेन यमक्षयम् ॥ २७/३१॥
इत्युक्तो रविजो मद्रान् नितरां पर्यकुत्सयत्।
शल्योऽपि सर्वदेशेषु नीचमध्योत्तमा नराः।
सन्तीत्युक्त्वाऽस्य सारथ्यं चक्रे पार्थहितेप्सया ॥ २७/३२॥
units.english:
When Karna spoke thus, Duryodhana requested Shalya to assume the charioteer-ship of Karna. Shalya acted as if he was angry. Duryodhana calmed him down, describing the greatness of charioteers over those who ride them.

“Only he who is better in intellect, strength, knowledge and courage than a rider should become the charioteer. Just like Krishna is to Arjuna and just as Brahma was to Shiva when the latter went to destroy Tripura”.

Shalya acted as if he was convinced with those and other words (of Duryodhana) and became the charioteer of Karna. Along with him, Karna placed his army in a vyuha.

While on the way to battle, Karna boasted out of pride and said – “I shall become pleased with anyone who shows me Arjuna and shall grant him unlimited wealth”.

When Karna said thus, Shalya ridiculed him and said – “The Nivatakavachas have been killed by Arjuna. The Khandava was burnt (by him). Which human can win against such a person? All of you have seen him during the Uttara-gograhana also”. Note: At the end of the thirteenth year of exile, Arjuna went with Uttara and rescued the cows of Virata, when the Kauravas had captured the cows on the northern side of Virata (Uttara- gograhana). At that time, he had single handedly defeated Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Krupa, Duryodhana and the rest.

“Like crows and jackals against Hamsa and Lions, do not go against Arjuna in battle. Do not get killed by him and reach Yamaloka” – when Shalya said thus Karna started incessantly berating the people of Madra country.

Shalya then replied saying every country has people who are low, average and excellent in nature. Keeping Arjuna’s well being in mind, he started charioteering Karna.

After that, Karna, being seated in the chariot driven by Shalya, reached the Pandava army and started hurting them from all sides with his arrows. Duryodhana, Krupa and the others and Ashwathama, that excellent knower of great astras, protected Karna in that battle.

units.sanskrit:
कर्णोऽपि शल्यनियतेन रथेन पार्थसेनामवाप्य विदुधाव शरैः समन्तात्।
संरक्षितो युधि सुयोधनगौतमाद्यैराचार्यजेन च महास्त्रविदां वरेण ॥ २७/३३॥
तं भीमपार्षतशिनिप्रवराभिगुप्ता सा पाण्डवेयपृतनाऽभिववर्ष बाणैः।
तां सूर्यसूनुरथ बाणवरैर्विदार्य सम्प्राद्रवच्छितशरैरपि धर्मसूनुम् ॥ २७/३४॥
कृत्वा तमाशु विरथं धनुरस्य कण्ठे सज्यं निधाय परुषा गिर आह चोच्चैः।

दृष्ट्वैव मारुतिरमुं भृशमातुतोद दुर्योधनं विरथकार्मुकमाशु कृत्वा ॥ २७/३५॥
तं प्राणसंशयगतं नृपतिं निरीक्ष्य कर्णं जगाद युधि मद्रपतिः प्रदर्श्य।
यस्यार्थमेष समरस्त्वमियं च सेना तं त्वं यमस्य सदनं प्रयियासुमद्य ॥ २७/३६॥
भीमेन पीडितममुं परिपाहि शीघ्रं किं ते युधिष्ठिरममुं हि मुधाऽभिपीड्य।
श्रुत्वाऽस्य वाक्यमतिहाय युधिष्ठिरं तं कर्णो ययौ नृपतिरक्षणतत्परोऽलम् ॥ २७/३७॥
दृष्ट्वैव तं पवनसूनुरभि त्वियाय क्रोधाद् दिधक्षुरिव कर्णममेयधामा।
राजावनाय शिनिपुङ्गवपार्षतौ च सन्दिश्य कर्णमभिगच्छत आस रूपम् ॥ २७/३८॥
अन्ते कृतान्तनरसिंहतनोर्यथैव विष्णोर्हरं ग्रसत आत्तसमस्तविश्‍वम्।
तद्वेगतः प्रतिचचाल धरा समस्ता विद्राविता च सकला प्रतिवीरसेना ॥ २७/३९॥
वैकर्तनेन शरसञ्चयताडितः स बाणं च वज्रसदृशं प्रमुमोच तस्मिन्।
तेनाहतो मृतकवत् स पपात कर्णो भीमः क्षुरं च जगृहेऽभिययौ च पद्भ्याम् ॥ २७/४०॥
units.english:
The Pandava army, well protected by Bhima, Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki, fought against Karna, showering him with arrows. Destroying that army with excellent arrows, Karna started hurting Yudhishthira badly with sharp arrows.

Karna quickly rendered Dharmaraja chariot-less and stuck his bow in his neck. He spoke cruel words against him in a loud voice. Seeing this, Bhima immediately caused Duryodhana to lose his chariot and also disarmed him. He started tormenting Duryodhana greatly.

Seeing Duryodhana in danger of losing his life, Shalya showed him to Karna and said – “For whom are you fighting this war? That person for whom you and your army exist is getting ready to go to Yama’s abode. Protect him immediately from Bhima’s torment. What is the purpose of such useless hurting of Yudhishthira?”. Listening to his words, Karna left Dharmaraja and rushed to protect the King.

As soon as he saw Karna, Bhima came against him like he was going to burn him in anger. Possessing immense radiance, Bhima sent Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki to protect Yudhishthira. When he rushed towards Karna, he appeared like Narasimha who swallows Shiva, after the latter has caused the destruction of the entire world during Pralaya. The Earth shook vigorously due to his speed and the enemy soldiers lost direction and ran away.

When he was hit by a cluster of arrows from Karna, Bhimasena picked up an arrow that was as hard as a diamond and released it against him. Hit by that arrow, Karna fell down like a corpse. Bhima picked up a sword and went towards Karna on foot.

units.sanskrit:
निन्दां हरेस्तु विदधाति परोक्षगोऽपि यस्तं प्रगृह्य करवाणि विजिह्वमेव।
एवं हि वायुतनयस्य सदा प्रतिज्ञा छेत्तुं स तेन रविजस्य ससार जिह्वाम् ॥ २७/४१॥
आयान्तमन्तिकममुं प्रसमीक्ष्य शल्यो नेत्याह हेतुभिरहो न मृषा प्रतिज्ञा।
कार्या त्वयैव पुरुहूतसुतस्य जिह्वां मा तेन पातय मरुत्सुत सूतसूनोः ॥ २७/४२॥
इत्युक्त्वा प्रमुखात् तस्य रथेनैव तु मद्रराट्।
वैकर्तनमपोवाह सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः ॥ २७/४३॥
जित्वा सूर्यसुतं भीमः कौरवाणामनीकिनीम्।
सर्वां विद्रावयामास द्रौणिदुर्योधनावृताम् ॥ २७/४४॥
अक्षौहिणीत्रयं तेन तदा विलुलितं क्षणात्।

तदैव गुरुपुत्रोऽयात् पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम् ॥ २७/४५॥
विमृद्य सकलां सेनां कृत्वा च विरथं नृपम्।
धृष्टद्युम्नं यमौ चैव सात्यकिं द्रौपदीसुतान्।
क्षणेन विरथीकृत्य सर्वांश्‍चक्रे निरायुधान् ॥ २७/४६॥
तान् भग्नदर्पान् रणतोऽपयातानन्वेव बाणावृतमन्तरिक्षम्।
कुर्वन् ययौ धर्मराजस्तमाह किं नः स्वधर्मे निरतान् विहंसि ॥ २७/४७॥
क्षत्रियान् परधर्मस्थो मा हिंसीरिति चोदितः।
प्रहस्य तान् विहायैव ययौ यत्राच्युतार्जुनौ ॥ २७/४८॥
units.english:
It was Bhima’s vow that he would cut off the tongue of the person who condemned Sri Hari, even if it was done indirectly. Therefore, he went towards Karna to cut his tongue.

Noticing Bhima approaching, Shalya stopped him with relevant justification and said – “Do not cause the vow of the son of Indra to go waste. Therefore O Bhima! Do not cut Karna’s tongue”. Note: Sri Vadiraja Tirtha explains that cutting the tongue of a Kshatriya like Karna would be equivalent to killing him since his self-pride would be destroyed.

Saying thus, Shalya drove off Karna, in front of everyone, away from Bhima to a distance.

Having defeated Karna, Bhimasena started scattering away the Kaurava army that included Duryodhana and Ashwathama.

Bhima had by then quickly destroyed three akshouhinis. At the same time, Ashwathama tore into the Pandava army.

Ashwathama destroyed the Pandava army and rendered Dharmaraja chariot-less. Facing Dhrishtadyumna, Nakula-Sahadeva, Satyaki and the sons of Draupadi, he quickly destroyed all their chariots and made them weapon-less.

Ashwathama started filling the sky with arrows even as Yudhishthira and the others, their ego damaged, started retreating. Dharmaraja asked him – “Why are you, one is practicing Paradharma, causing pain to those of us Kshatriyas who are engaged in Swadharma? Do not harm us in this way”. When Dharmaraja spoke thus, Ashwathama laughed loudly and proceeded to where Sri Achyuta and Arjuna were present.

units.sanskrit:
संशप्तकैस्तत्र संयुद्ध्यमानं समाह्वयामास सुरेन्द्रसूनुम्।
स बाणयुक्तं भुजगेन्द्रकल्पमुन्नम्य बाहुं युधये सुशूरम् ॥ २७/४९॥
पार्थः संशप्तकगणैः संसृष्टः समरार्थिभिः।
आहूतो द्रौणिना चैव कार्यं कृष्णमपृच्छत।
चोदयामास च हयान् कृष्णो द्रौणिरथं प्रति ॥ २७/५०॥
उभौ च तावस्त्रविदां प्रधानौ महाबलौ संयति जातदर्पौ।
शरैः समस्ताः प्रदिशो दिशश्‍च द्रोणेन्द्रसूनू तिमिराः प्रचक्रतुः ॥ २७/५१॥
द्रौणिस्तदा स्यन्दनवाजिरोमस्वरोमकूपध्वजकार्मुकेभ्यः।
शरानमोघान् सततं सृजानो बबन्ध पार्थं शरपञ्जरेण ॥ २७/५२॥
तस्मिन् निबद्धे हरिरप्रमेयो विबोधयामास सुरेन्द्रसूनुम्।
आलिङ्गनेनास्य ददौ बलं च स उत्थितोऽस्त्राण्यमुचन्महान्ति ॥ २७/५३॥
निवार्य तानस्त्रवरैर्गुरोः सुतश्‍चिच्छेद च ज्यां युधि गाण्डिवस्य।
ववर्ष पार्थं च शरैरथान्या ज्याऽऽसीत् तया गाण्डिवं सोऽप्ययुङ्क्त ॥ २७/५४॥
ततः शरेण कुपितः शितेन द्रौणिसारथेः।
शिरो जहार कौन्तेयः सारथ्यं सोऽकरोत् स्वयम् ॥ २७/५५॥
शरान् विसृजता तेन सारथ्यमपि कुर्वता।
शरकूटेन पार्थः स पुनर्बद्धो द्विजन्मना ॥ २७/५६॥
units.english:
Once there, even as Arjuna, the son of Indra and great hero, was fighting the Samshaptakas, Ashwathama held up his arrow-wielding shoulders that were like a great snake and invited him to battle.

Arjuna, who was fighting the group of war-mongering Samshaptakas, asked Sri Krishna what his duty was when Ashwathama invited him. Sri Krishna drove the horses towards Ashwathama. Note: Arjuna was put in a quandary when two sets of people desired to engage him in battle. He was fighting the Samshaptakas already when Ashwathama invited him. Hence he took refuge in the wisdom of Sri Krishna.

Arjuna and Ashwathama, the chief amongst knowers of astras, immensely powerful and ones who swayed with pride, caused darkness in all directions with their arrows in that battle.

Ashwathama then rained such a shower of arrows that they came out relentlessly from the chariot, hairs of the horses, his own hair strands, flag and the bow. He then tied Arjuna in a cage of arrows. Note: Ashwathama was firing so many arrows that it appeared, to onlookers, as if arrows were emanating from the chariot, hair of the horses and the hairs on Ashwathama’s body.

When Arjuna was tied up thus, Sri Krishna, one who cannot be comprehended, advised him. He also gave him a hug that increased his strength. Arjuna came out of it and started executing great astras.

Ashwathama relieved those astras with excellent astras of his own and cut off the string of the Gandiva. He showered many arrows too at Arjuna. Immediately, a new string appeared on the Gandiva and Arjuna tied the same.

After that, an angry Arjuna caused the head of Ashwathama’s charioteer to fly by aiming a sharp arrow at him. Ashwathama then started charioteering his own vehicle.

Releasing arrows, while simultaneously riding the vehicle, Ashwathama once again tied up Arjuna with a cluster of arrows.

units.sanskrit:
पुनरालिङ्ग्य  कृष्णस्तमधाच्छत्रुविघातकम्।
बलमस्मिंस्ततः पार्थ उत्तस्थौ शरचापभृत् ॥ २७/५७॥
ववर्ष च शरान् भूयो द्रोणपुत्रेऽरिमर्दनः।
पुनस्तस्य तुतोद ज्यां द्रौणिः सन्धाय तां पुनः ॥ २७/५८॥
पार्थो द्रोणसुतस्याश्‍वरश्मींश्‍चिच्छेद सायकैः।
विरश्मयो हया द्रौणेः पुनः पार्थशराहताः ॥ २७/५९॥
अपोहुर्दूरमेवास्मात् सोऽपि सन्धाय तान् पुनः।
चिन्तयामास नैतस्मादधिकं शक्यतेऽर्जुने ॥ २७/६०॥
सारथित्वात् केशवस्य ध्वजस्थत्वाद्धनूमतः।
गाण्डिवत्वात् कार्मुकस्य चेषुध्योरक्षयत्वतः ॥ २७/६१॥
अवध्यत्वात् तथाऽश्‍वानामभेद्यत्वाद् रथस्य च।
अतो योद्धुं समर्थोऽपि नाद्य यामि धनञ्जयम् ॥ २७/६२॥
एवं स मत्वा प्रविवेश सेनां पाण्डोः सुतानामथ तं समभ्ययात्।
पाण्ड्यस्तयोरास सुयुद्धमद्भुतं प्रवर्षतोः सायकपूगमुग्रम् ॥ २७/६३॥
अष्टावष्टशतान्यूहुः शकटानि यदायुधम्।
अह्नस्तदष्टभागेन द्रौणिश्‍चिच्छेद तत्र हि ॥ २७/६४॥
units.english:
Sri Krishna once again hugged Arjuna and gave him strength that could destroy enemies. Arjuna came out of that entrapment and picked up his bow and arrows.

Arjuna, the destroyer of enemies, once again rained arrows on Ashwathama. In turn, Ashwathama once again cut off Gandiva’s string. Arjuna tied it back again and cut off the ropes that were holding Ashwathama’s horses.

Without the ropes (to contain), Ashwathama’s horses ran away afar being tormented by Arjuna’s arrows. Ashwathama brought them under control again and thought to himself – “It is not possible to go more than this against Arjuna”.

“Sri Krishna is his charioteer. Hanuman sits in his mast. His bow is Gandiva. His quivers never get exhausted. Similarly his horses cannot be killed and his chariot cannot be destroyed. Therefore, although capable, I shall not proceed against Arjuna (any further) now”.

Thinking thus, Ashwathama entered the Pandava formation. The King of Pandya came to face him. An amazing great battle took place between them. Both of them showered terrible clusters of arrows.

Ashwathama, in one eighth of the day, released arrows that were carried over eight carriages each driven by eight oxen. Note: Ashwathama was so furious in war on that day that he exhausted arrows that had been carried in eight carriages, each of which were pulled by eight oxen. And he exhausted all these arrows in just one eighth of the day!

units.sanskrit:
अथ तं विरथं कृत्वा छित्वा कार्मुकमाहवे।
सकुण्डलं शिरो द्रौणिर्जहार मुकुटोज्ज्वलम् ॥ २७/६५॥
अथ विद्रावयामास पृतनां पाण्डवीं शरैः।
तदा जघान पार्थोऽपि दण्डधाराख्यमागधम् ॥ २७/६६॥
विद्राव्यमाणां पृतनां निरीक्ष्य गुरोः सुतेनाभ्यगमत् त्वरावान्।
धृष्टद्युम्नस्तं स ऊचे सुपापं हनिष्ये त्वामद्य युद्धे गुरुघ्नम् ॥ २७/६७॥
इत्युक्तो दर्शयामास पार्षतः खड्गमुत्तमम्।
अयं तव पितुर्हन्ता वदिष्यति तवोत्तरम् ॥ २७/६८॥
इत्युक्त्वा धनुरादाय ववर्ष च शरान् बहून्।
तयोः समभवद् युद्धं तुमुलं रोमहर्षणम् ॥ २७/६९॥
तत्र तं पार्षतं द्रौणिः क्षणेन विरथायुधम्।
कृत्वाऽन्ताय शरांस्तीक्ष्णान् मुमोच नच तस्य ते ॥ २७/७०॥
त्वचं च चिच्छिदुर्द्रौणिः खड्गहस्तोऽभिजग्मिवान्।
खड्गेन सोऽस्त्रशस्त्रैरप्यनिर्भिण्णत्वचं तदा ॥ २७/७१॥
मौर्व्या ममन्थ धनुषः पातयित्वा धरातले।

आकृष्यमाणं पार्षतं तं दृष्ट्वा कृष्णप्रचोदितः ॥ २७/७२॥
units.english:
After that, Ashwathama, rendering him chariot-less, broke his bow and cut off his head that was resplendent with a crown and ear-rings.

Ashwathama started disintegrating the Pandava army with his arrows. Arjuna then killed one of the Kings of Magadha country by name Dandadhara.

Watching his army being chased away by Ashwathama, Dhrishtadyumna came there hurriedly. Ashwathama said to him – “I shall kill you in battle today for you are a great sinner, having killed the Guru”.

When he said thus, Dhrishtadyumna showed him his excellent sword and said – “This sword which killed your father shall answer you”.

Replying thus, Dhrishtadyumna picked up his bow and showered many arrows. An hair-raising duel took place between them on equal terms.

Ashwathama quickly rendered Dhrishtadyumna chariot-less and weapon-less. He shot many arrows at Dhrishtadyumna, wanting to kill him, but they did not even cut his skin. Ashwathama picked up a sword and pounced on him. Even with the sword and other weapons, his skin did not suffer any wounds. He then dragged him on to the ground and started pulling him with his bow.

Seeing Dhrishtadyumna being pulled in that manner, Partha and Bhima, impelled by Sri Krishna, started hitting him (Ashwathama) from both sides.

units.sanskrit:
पार्थो भीमश्‍चोभयतः शरैरभिविजघ्नतुः।
स ताभ्यां वज्रसमितैः शरैरभिहतो भृशम् ॥ २७/७३॥
विसृज्य पार्षतं स्वीयमारुरोह रथं पुनः।

जगाम च ततोऽन्यत्र पाञ्चाल्योऽपि रथं पुनः ॥ २७/७४॥
आरुह्यान्यं स्वात्तधन्वा कृतवर्माणमभ्ययात्।
तयोरासीत् सुतुमुलं युद्धमद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥ २७/७५॥
तत्र नातिप्रयत्नेन पाञ्चाल्यो विरथायुधम्।
चकार कृतवर्माणं तमपोवाह गौतमः ॥ २७/७६॥
अथ दुर्योधनो राजा माद्रेयावभ्ययाद् रणे।
ताभ्यां तस्याभवद् युद्धं घोरमद्भुतदर्शनम्।
तत्र नातिप्रयत्नेन तेन तौ विरथीकृतौ ॥ २७/७७॥
स्वयं युधिष्ठिरो राजा तदा तं समवारयत्।
व्यश्‍वसूतध्वजं चक्रे तं च दुर्योधनो रणे ॥ २७/७८॥
अथागतं सूर्यसुतं पुनश्‍च जगाम भीमो रभसो रथेन।
दुर्योधनं चास्य समक्षमेव चकार वीरो विरथं क्षणेन ॥ २७/७९॥
निवार्य कर्णं च शरैरमुष्य सूनोः सुषेणस्य शिरश्‍चकर्त।
पपात भूमौ स पितुः समीपे यथा हतः सत्यसेनोऽमुनैव।
यथैव कर्णावरजौ पुरैव निशायुद्धे कर्णपुरः प्रपातितौ ॥ २७/८०॥
units.english:
Being hit by the two of them with arrows that were hard as diamonds, Ashwathama let go off Dhrishtadyumna and climbed his chariot again. Ashwathama proceeded elsewhere from there. Dhrishtadyumna too climbed another chariot and, lifting his bow, went against Krutavarma.

The duel between Dhrishtadyumna and Krutavarma was amazing to watch. In that fight, Dhrishtadyumna, without much exertion, rendered Krutavarma weapon-less and chariot-less. Krupa took Krutavarma elsewhere from there.

Thereafter Duryodhana fought against Nakula and Sahadeva from his chariot. An amazing and terrifying battle took place between them. Without much effort, Duryodhana destroyed the chariots of those two.

King Yudhishthira then himself faced Duryodhana, who destroyed his horses, charioteer and flags in battle.

The brave Bhimasena faced Karna, who returned by then, and proceeded further. Right in front of him (Karna) Bhima rendered Duryodhana chariot-less.
